preferred_term: jack stud
issue: Australian public sources used here define a jack stud as a shortened stud above or below an opening, while some industry material uses jack or trimmer stud for a member supporting a lintel end.
next_action: Check terminology in licensed AS 1684 content and current Australian framing manuals before accepting any equivalence.

preferred_term: jamb stud
issue: King stud is common North American terminology but was not established as the preferred Australian term by the sources used.
next_action: Survey Australian training and manufacturer documents from several states before classifying the regional alias.

preferred_term: lintel
issue: Header can mean a lintel in North American usage, but may also mean a non-loadbearing trimmer or another cross-member.
next_action: Do not use header as an automatic search or drawing synonym until the intended role is known.

preferred_term: head trimmer
issue: Both can occur at the head of an opening, but a lintel is a structural spanning member while a head trimmer may only form and fix the rough opening.
next_action: Keep separate roles; confirm state and trade usage with additional Australian references.

preferred_term: jack rafter
issue: Creeper may be used for some shortened rafters, but the exact regional boundary between the terms is not established by the pilot sources.
next_action: Gather Australian roof-carpentry references from multiple training providers before treating the terms as synonyms.

preferred_term: rim board or boundary joist
issue: The edge member of a platform floor is real, but preferred naming and whether rim board and boundary joist are the same object depend on the floor system.
next_action: Add only after separately researching solid-timber floors, I-joist floors and proprietary floor systems.

preferred_term: truss bracing
issue: Speedbrace is a product or proprietary usage, not a generic object class for every form of truss bracing.
next_action: Retain only as a proprietary search term and never use it as the canonical object name.

preferred_term: foundation material
issue: NCC footing diagrams use foundation for the supporting ground, while everyday building speech often uses foundation for the constructed footing or slab system.
next_action: Require context whenever a command says only foundation; do not map it automatically to either soil or concrete work.

preferred_term: stiffened raft slab
issue: Raft slab is often used broadly for an integral slab foundation and does not reliably distinguish a stiffened raft from a waffle raft or another raft arrangement.
next_action: Treat raft slab as a family-level search term and ask for the structural arrangement before generating geometry.

preferred_term: waffle raft slab
issue: Waffle slab can describe the residential ground-supported pod system or a suspended two-way ribbed slab, which have different hosts and load paths.
next_action: Require ground-supported versus suspended context before resolving the short term waffle slab.

preferred_term: under-slab damp-proofing membrane
issue: The Housing Provisions use both names in the slab context, but wider building-science usage can distinguish damp-proofing, vapour control and waterproofing functions.
next_action: Accept vapour barrier only when the context is the membrane directly beneath a residential slab-on-ground.

preferred_term: strip footing
issue: Legacy training material notes overlapping usage in some footing-slab arrangements, but an edge beam is normally integral with or attached to a slab edge while a strip footing is a continuous footing role.
next_action: Keep separate canonical roles and use the concrete pour and slab connection as disambiguating context.

preferred_term: slab void former
issue: A waffle pod is a particular box-like void former used in a waffle raft; void former is a broader class that includes other shapes and materials.
next_action: Preserve the parent-child relationship and do not use the two terms as universal exact synonyms.

preferred_term: controlled fill
issue: Both are compacted fill, but the Housing Provisions define them as different placement and compaction categories with different application limits.
next_action: Keep separate objects and require the documented fill category when a tool records or quantifies under-slab fill.

preferred_term: subsoil drain
issue: Ag drain is common trade language and French drain is a broader international configuration; neither term alone proves the exact pipe, aggregate and filter arrangement.
next_action: Research Australian plumbing and civil guidance before promoting either term to an exact synonym.

preferred_term: termite management system
issue: A barrier may be only one component; the NCC explicitly warns that components such as a concrete slab need integration with other details to form a complete system.
next_action: Never infer whole-system coverage from the presence of one barrier component in a model.

preferred_term: stormwater detention or retention tank
issue: The vessels can look alike, but detention, retention and rainwater reuse describe different storage and outlet functions that may coexist in one product.
next_action: Split configured tank roles during the full stormwater and plumbing pass and retain shared physical product mappings separately.

preferred_term: vertical masonry articulation joint
issue: The terms overlap in trade usage, but the Housing Provisions also use control-joint language for junctions between different masonry materials, so an automatic synonym could produce the wrong joint geometry.
next_action: Keep movement purpose, orientation and material-junction context explicit before resolving control joint to an object.

preferred_term: masonry damp-proof course
issue: The same sheet product can perform both roles, but a DPC interrupts capillary moisture while a flashing collects and drains water along a shaped path.
next_action: Retain separate role objects and allow one modelled product instance to carry both roles only when the detail supports both.

preferred_term: masonry perpend
issue: A weephole is commonly formed by deliberately leaving a perpend open, but an ordinary filled perpend is a mortar joint and must not be treated as a drainage opening.
next_action: Model the weephole as an opening state at a selected perpend location, never as the default state of every perpend.

preferred_term: concrete masonry block
issue: Besser is widely used in Australian speech for concrete blockwork but originates as a proprietary name and does not identify every concrete masonry block product.
next_action: Retain Besser block as a proprietary search term only; generate a generic concrete masonry block unless a product is explicitly selected.

preferred_term: masonry veneer wall
issue: Both use a framed wall and a single masonry leaf, but conventional masonry veneer puts the leaf outside the frame as the weather skin while reverse veneer puts it inside for exposed thermal mass.
next_action: Require inside-versus-outside leaf position before generating veneer geometry.

preferred_term: cold-formed steel framing
issue: Both are steel structures, but residential light-gauge members are formed from thin sheet and commonly follow NASH or AS/NZS 4600, while structural steel members such as universal beams and columns use different sections, connections and design pathways.
next_action: Require light-gauge versus hot-rolled or hollow-section context before choosing a steel member family.

preferred_term: steel wall top track or bottom track
issue: Australian steel-frame sources use both plate and track language, but proprietary systems can distinguish section forms and functions at the wall head and base.
next_action: Accept plate as a search synonym but preserve the selected system's top-track and bottom-track product identities.

preferred_term: steel floor boundary joist
issue: All terms can describe a floor-edge member, but the physical section and whether it behaves as a joist, track or proprietary cassette edge vary by system.
next_action: Use boundary member as the family role and obtain the exact section and connection from the frame supplier.

preferred_term: prefabricated steel floor cassette
issue: A ladder frame is one parallel-rail and cross-member configuration; floor cassette is a broader prefabricated module and can use other layouts.
next_action: Store ladder as a cassette-layout attribute unless the selected proprietary system establishes it as a separate product object.

preferred_term: steel framing self-drilling screw or masonry anchor
issue: Tek and Dynabolt are proprietary or genericised trade names and do not identify every compatible screw or anchor product.
next_action: Keep both as search terms only and require product, substrate, coating and connection schedule before drawing or counting a specific fastener.

preferred_term: structural member role plus section designation
candidate_term: beam, column or bearer used as a section name
issue: A role tells what the member does, while UB, UC, PFC, RHS and other section designations tell its cross-sectional form. Everyday speech often collapses the two and can select the wrong geometry or load-path object.
next_action: Make future drawing commands resolve both role and profile; never infer UC merely from column or UB merely from beam.

preferred_term: specified Australian section designation
issue: I-beam describes a broad shape and RSJ is ambiguous trade shorthand. Neither reliably distinguishes UB, UC, TFB, WB or an older or imported section family.
next_action: Treat I-beam and RSJ as search prompts that require a section designation, dimensions or verified existing-building record before geometry is generated.

preferred_term: column base plate connection
issue: Base plate can mean the single steel plate or casually mean the full column-to-support assembly including welds, anchors, nuts, washers, grout and substrate interface.
next_action: Keep the plate and connection assembly as separate objects; ask whether a command intends only the plate or the installed base assembly.

preferred_term: structural bolt or anchor bolt according to function
issue: A member-to-member structural bolt passes through connected steel plies, while an anchor bolt connects a base plate into concrete or masonry. Their hosts, geometry and installation data differ.
next_action: Use connection context and substrate to resolve the bolt family before drawing, scheduling or counting it.

preferred_term: designed structural steel member web penetration
issue: Service hole can mean a factory-punched opening in light-gauge framing or a separately designed cut-out in a hot-rolled member web. The same short term must not authorise either geometry automatically.
next_action: Require the host member family and approved opening schedule before resolving service hole to a drawable opening.

preferred_term: roof sarking when the pliable layer performs the roof-underlay role
candidate_term: sarking, underlay, vapour barrier or reflective insulation
issue: These words can describe overlapping products but not the same installed function. A pliable roof underlay may manage water, air, vapour and radiation differently according to its classification, laps, ventilation and roof assembly.
next_action: Resolve the product classification and intended control functions before drawing layer direction, taped joints, ventilation gaps or claiming it is a vapour barrier.

preferred_term: profiled metal roof sheet
issue: COLORBOND is a proprietary prepainted steel product family, not the generic name for every metal roof sheet, profile, base metal, coating or complete roof assembly.
next_action: Treat Colorbond as a product or finish cue; still require profile, thickness, coating, sheet length, fixing system and manufacturer compatibility.

preferred_term: corrugated metal roof sheet with specified material and coating
issue: Common Australian speech preserves historical material names even when the installed sheet is usually coated steel. The slang does not confirm the base metal, coating, thickness or profile dimensions.
next_action: Use the slang for search and recognition only; require a scheduled product or measured existing profile before generating exact geometry or material data.

preferred_term: flashing or capping according to junction and water-shedding role
issue: Both are folded weathering pieces and some details combine the roles. Capping usually covers an exposed ridge, hip, barge or parapet edge, while flashing bridges or drains a junction, abutment or penetration.
next_action: Classify the object from its host junction, cross-section and drainage role, while retaining the alternate word as a search cue where industry usage overlaps.

preferred_term: valley gutter for the formed water-carrying channel
candidate_term: roof valley, valley gutter or valley flashing
issue: Roof valley can mean the geometric intersection line, while valley gutter and valley flashing can both refer to the formed piece under the cut roof coverings. Geometry and function must be separated.
next_action: Use valley gutter for the drawable channel, store the roof-valley line as geometry, and use valley flashing as a related search term unless a source defines a distinct detail.

preferred_term: mortar bedding and flexible pointing as separate ridge or hip components
issue: Bedding supports and seats capping tiles, while pointing finishes and seals the exposed edges. A single casual phrase can hide two materials with different geometry and maintenance behaviour.
next_action: Generate bedding and pointing as separate continuous components around the capping tile and preserve the chosen mechanical fixing or clip as another object.

preferred_term: gutter outlet
issue: Trade and regional words vary for the fitting that transfers normal gutter flow to a downpipe. Nozzle can also mean an overflow device, so the short word does not establish normal-flow versus overflow function.
next_action: Ask whether the fitting is the normal downpipe outlet or a dedicated overflow; then resolve its host face, throat, level, shape and connected object.

preferred_term: rainhead for the external visible collection box and box gutter sump for the internal depressed collector
issue: Both receive gutter water and feed an outlet, but their position and failure behaviour differ. A rainhead relieves surcharge visibly outside; a box gutter sump is part of an internal gutter system and needs an independently resolved overflow path.
next_action: Resolve inside-versus-outside location, incoming gutter, outlet and overflow route before selecting geometry or making a substitution.

preferred_term: soaker gutter for a continuous concealed channel and soaker tray flashing for a local penetration or abutment tray
candidate_term: soaker, soaker tray or soaker gutter
issue: The words overlap in roofing practice. A continuous narrow drainage channel differs from a local tray flashing and from individual soakers placed beneath small-unit roof coverings.
next_action: Use path length, host, inlet edges and discharge point to choose the continuous gutter or local flashing object; add individual tile soakers only after a primary source confirms their distinct geometry.

preferred_term: downpipe above ground and stormwater drain below ground
issue: Stormwater pipe can casually mean either the visible roof-water leader or the buried drain. The two have different supports, fittings, geometry, inspection needs and relationships to the building.
next_action: Resolve above-ground versus buried location and use the adaptor as the explicit transition between the two systems.

preferred_term: cladding material plus board profile
issue: Weatherboard describes a wall-cladding form but does not establish whether the board is solid timber, fibre cement, exterior hardboard or another proprietary material. Those materials have different cuts, fixings, joints and finishes.
next_action: Treat weatherboard as a form cue and require the material or product family before selecting geometry, cutting rules, fixings or coating.

preferred_term: exterior hardboard or fibre cement according to the product
issue: Masonite is genericised proprietary language often used for hardboard, while cement sheet is loose trade language usually aimed at fibre cement. Neither word proves the product standard, exterior grade or exact material.
next_action: Use product evidence or material schedule to resolve hardboard versus fibre cement before drawing edges, joints, fasteners or finishes.

preferred_term: board, sheet or structural panel according to geometry and role
issue: Panel is used casually for broad sheets, factory panels and complete facade modules. A long narrow board, a thin fixed sheet and a reinforced AAC panel have different support, joint and load behaviour.
next_action: Resolve unit width-to-length form, thickness, material, reinforcement and support method before assigning an object class.

preferred_term: direct-fixed wall arrangement or face-fixed fastener according to context
issue: Direct fix describes the wall build-up without a drained cavity. Face fix describes where a fastener passes through the visible cladding face. A direct-fixed wall can still use concealed board edges, and cavity cladding can be face-fixed.
next_action: Store wall build-up and fastener visibility as separate properties; never infer one from the other.

preferred_term: cladding drainage cavity when referring to the clear space behind lightweight cladding
issue: Cavity can also mean a masonry wall cavity, while rainscreen may describe a broader pressure-moderated or ventilated facade concept. The short words do not define depth, drainage, ventilation, fire barriers or closures.
next_action: Resolve the wall system, boundary layers, clear path, openings and barriers before generating cavity geometry.

preferred_term: external wall weather barrier with stated water, air and vapour classifications
candidate_term: wall wrap, sarking or vapour barrier
issue: Wall wrap and sarking are common product-family words. Vapour barrier claims a particular vapour-control function that may be wrong for the selected membrane, climate and wall build-up.
next_action: Require membrane classification, location and intended control functions before treating the layer as a vapour barrier or choosing which seams and penetrations are sealed.

preferred_term: cladding movement joint assembly
candidate_term: control joint, expansion joint or H flashing
issue: Control and expansion joint describe movement roles, while an H-shaped profile may be only one joining or flashing component. The visible trim does not prove gap width, support separation, backing, sealant or drainage.
next_action: Model the movement gap and weathering assembly first, then attach the selected H profile, flashing or cover as a component.

preferred_term: corner flashing behind and corner trim at the visible face
candidate_term: corner mould, corner angle or corner flashing
issue: A visible corner trim finishes cladding edges; a concealed corner flashing supplies secondary weather protection. One folded angle can sometimes perform both roles, but they should not be collapsed without the detail.
next_action: Resolve visibility, position relative to the membrane, water path and edge-receiving profile before choosing flashing, trim or a combined product.

preferred_term: reinforced AAC panel or unreinforced AAC block according to product and structure
issue: Hebel is proprietary language and AAC names a material family. Reinforced external panels and unreinforced blocks differ in reinforcement, unit geometry, supports, joints and applicable system documentation.
next_action: Require the supplied system and confirm panel versus block construction before generating units, joints, cuts or fixings.

preferred_term: solid metal sheet wall cladding when using the AS 1562.1 pathway
candidate_term: metal panel or aluminium composite panel
issue: The NCC guidance distinguishes solid metal sheeting from laminated and composite metal panels. Similar facade appearance does not place a composite panel within the solid-sheet DTS pathway.
next_action: Require product construction and evidence of suitability; do not map composite or laminated panels to solid metal sheet objects or AS 1562.1 automatically.

preferred_term: eaves or soffit lining according to the underside area being closed
candidate_term: eaves sheet, soffit sheet or fibro
issue: The first two terms often identify the same external underside role, while fibro is legacy trade language that may imply fibre cement but does not establish a non-asbestos product, thickness or product standard.
next_action: Use location to resolve eaves versus soffit and require verified product identity before assigning fibre-cement material, especially in existing buildings.

preferred_term: window perimeter frame or rough wall opening framing according to context
issue: Window frame usually means the factory product around the sashes and glass, but builders may use the phrase for studs, lintel and trimmers forming the wall opening. These are separate assemblies with different geometry and load paths.
next_action: Ask whether the command means the manufactured fenestration frame or the structural rough-opening framing before drawing or measuring it.

preferred_term: window sash for a moving framed window part and door leaf or panel for a moving door part
issue: A sash is the framed moving or fixed glazed part of a window. Panel is broader and can mean a glass pane, door panel, fixed field or complete infill. Interchanging them loses hardware, track and perimeter-member meaning.
next_action: Resolve window versus door, moving versus fixed, and framed component versus bare glass before assigning the term.

preferred_term: window sill or door threshold according to the opening
issue: A window sill is the lower horizontal frame member and drainage zone. A door threshold is the trafficable lower frame component. Both can be called sill in product language, but clearance, accessibility, track and weathering geometry differ.
next_action: Use the host opening and whether people cross it to resolve sill versus threshold; retain manufacturer naming as an alias.

preferred_term: frame mullion, coupling mullion, meeting stile or interlock stile according to role
issue: A frame mullion divides fixed frame bays, a coupling mullion joins separate units, and meeting or interlock stiles are edge members on moving sashes or door panels. They can align visually but have different hosts and connections.
next_action: Resolve fixed frame versus moving panel and whether the member divides one product or couples two products before generating the profile.

preferred_term: fixed glazed light, fixed sash or fixed window assembly according to construction level
issue: A fixed window is the complete product. A fixed light is the non-opening glazed field. Some products hold that field directly in the main frame while others use a non-operating sash, so visual immobility does not identify the component structure.
next_action: Ask whether the command targets the complete installed window or only one non-opening glazed field, then obtain the product detail for direct glazing versus fixed sash.

preferred_term: insect flyscreen, security screen or fall-protection screen according to tested function
issue: These products may all look like framed mesh. An ordinary flyscreen excludes insects but does not automatically provide security or resist the window-fall loads required of a protection screen.
next_action: Require the intended function and product evidence; never promote an insect screen to a security or fall-protection role from appearance.

preferred_term: opening weatherseal, glazing gasket or wall-opening perimeter seal according to interface
issue: A sash weatherseal seals moving frame edges, a glazing gasket cushions and seals glass inside a rebate, and the perimeter seal closes the installed frame-to-wall joint. Combining them produces wrong routes and quantities.
next_action: Resolve the two surfaces being sealed—moving panel to frame, glass to rebate, or window frame to wall—before selecting a seal object.

preferred_term: glass pane for one cut piece, IGU lite for one pane within a sealed unit, and glazed light for a framed field
issue: The words overlap in trade speech but represent different hierarchy levels. A pane is one glass body, a lite is its position in an IGU, and a light can be the complete glazed area bounded by frame members.
next_action: Store bare glass, its make-up position and the framed field as separate objects even when a schedule uses one word for all three.

preferred_term: certified safety-glazing product with its specific make-up
candidate_term: safety glass, toughened glass or laminated glass
issue: Safety glass is a performance classification, while toughened and laminated describe product construction. Not every laminated make-up is automatically the required safety product, and heat-strengthened monolithic glass is not the same as toughened safety glass.
next_action: Require product classification, make-up and permanent identification before assigning safety performance or substituting one construction for another.

preferred_term: insulating glass unit when panes, spacer and sealed cavity are manufactured as one unit
issue: Double glazing commonly means a two-lite IGU, but can also be used loosely for secondary glazing or two separate window layers. Those arrangements have different frames, cavities, seals, replacement units and thermal models.
next_action: Ask whether the panes share one sealed spacer-and-edge-seal unit; if not, research the separate secondary-glazing assembly before mapping it.

preferred_term: frame installation packer, glass setting block, glass location block or IGU spacer according to position and load
issue: All are small separating components, but a frame packer transfers installation reactions to the wall, a setting block carries glass weight, a location block maintains edge clearance and an IGU spacer forms the sealed cavity perimeter.
next_action: Use the component's two contact surfaces and whether it carries frame load, glass weight, glass location or cavity spacing to resolve the object.

preferred_term: low-emissivity coating on a specified glass surface
issue: Low-e glass is convenient product language, but the performance comes from a coating on a nominated face. Pane reversal, lamination and IGU surface numbering can move the coating to an exposed or incompatible location.
next_action: Store base glass and coating as separate linked objects and require the numbered surface or product make-up before generating section layers.

preferred_term: waterproof or water resistant according to the required performance and location
issue: The Housing Provisions use waterproof and water resistant as different performance requirements. Trade descriptions such as sealed or wet-area rated do not identify which performance applies or which physical layer provides it.
next_action: Store the required performance and protected extent separately for every surface; do not infer a membrane across every area described only as water resistant.

preferred_term: wet-area waterproofing system for the complete assembly and membrane for one waterproof layer
issue: A complete system also includes its compatible substrate, preparation, bond breakers, junction treatments, flashings, penetration seals, drain connection and terminations. Treating membrane as the whole system hides those drawable failure points.
next_action: Model the membrane as a part of a selected system and require all documented substrate, junction, penetration, drainage and termination components.

preferred_term: internal or external wet-area membrane according to its position relative to the tile bed
issue: In the Housing Provisions wet-area details, internal and external can describe whether the membrane is above or below the screed or tile bed. In general construction language the same words often mean inside or outside the building.
next_action: Ask whether internal or external refers to building location or layer order, then store the membrane's exact position in the assembly.

preferred_term: preformed shower base unit or in-situ shower tray assembly according to construction
candidate_term: shower tray, shower base or shower pan
issue: A preformed base is a manufactured vessel with an outlet and upturns. An in-situ tray is site-built from substrate, falls, membrane, edge details and finish. The shared trade terms do not reveal which geometry and interfaces are required.
next_action: Resolve manufactured versus site-built construction before generating the base, outlet, support, upturn, membrane and finish layers.

preferred_term: shower hob, waterstop angle or trafficable threshold according to physical role
issue: A hob is a raised kerb, a waterstop is a membrane termination that limits water migration, and a threshold is the trafficable doorway or shower crossing. They can occur together or align in plan but are not interchangeable.
next_action: Identify whether the object raises the edge, terminates the membrane, or forms a traffic crossing; draw separate coincident components when it performs more than one role.

preferred_term: shower stepdown for the finished level change and slab set-down for a structural recess
issue: A finished shower stepdown may be created by screed and finish levels, while a slab set-down is formed in the structural concrete. Using one term for both can cut structure unnecessarily or omit the required finished threshold geometry.
next_action: Store structural substrate levels separately from screed, membrane, tile and finished-surface levels, then derive the visible step from the complete build-up.

preferred_term: floor waste assembly, floor-waste gully or linear drain according to plumbing and geometry
candidate_term: floor drain, waste, grate or gully
issue: These words may describe the complete drainage fitting, only its visible grate, a trapped plumbing gully, or a long channel. Each has different body, outlet, membrane connection and fall geometry.
next_action: Resolve point versus linear geometry, trapped plumbing function, visible grate and concealed body before creating falls or connecting the membrane.

preferred_term: drainage flange or puddle flange according to the selected fitting and system detail
candidate_term: puddle flange, leak-control flange or drain flange
issue: The names overlap across standards, plumbing products and waterproofing trades. A flange may clamp, bond or receive the membrane at a different height and may provide openings for water within a tile bed.
next_action: Require the actual fitting profile, membrane level, outlet or riser arrangement and proprietary system detail rather than selecting a flange from its name alone.

preferred_term: fall-forming screed or tile bed according to the layer's job
issue: A screed establishes levels and falls; a tile bed supports the tiled finish. One mortar layer can perform both jobs, but a structural slab may already form falls or another layer may separate the functions.
next_action: Record each physical layer once, attach both roles if applicable, and keep its position relative to membrane, substrate, drain and tile explicit.

preferred_term: bond breaker for movement isolation and reinforcement band for membrane strengthening
candidate_term: corner tape, bond-breaker tape or reinforcing tape
issue: The products can all look like narrow rolls at corners. A bond breaker prevents three-sided adhesion or isolates movement, while reinforcement is embedded to strengthen or control membrane thickness. One proprietary strip may be approved for both, but the functions remain distinct.
next_action: Store function, route and membrane-system approval; allow one product instance to fulfil two linked roles only where its evidence supports both.

preferred_term: tile grout, flexible sealant joint and waterproof membrane as separate layers
candidate_term: waterproof grout, silicone or tile waterproofing
issue: Grout fills regular tile joints, flexible sealant accommodates movement at selected junctions, and the membrane provides the concealed waterproof layer. Marketing language about waterproof grout does not turn a tiled finish into the complete required waterproofing system.
next_action: Generate regular grout joints, scheduled flexible joints and the protected membrane field independently; never infer concealed compliance from the visible tile finish.

preferred_term: tile edge trim or waterstop angle according to hidden waterproofing role
candidate_term: tile angle, trim or aluminium angle
issue: A tile trim protects and finishes an exposed tile edge. A waterstop angle terminates or returns the waterproofing. Similar extruded profiles can align at a doorway or shower edge, but the visible trim is not automatically the waterstop.
next_action: Ask whether the profile connects to the membrane or only finishes the tile edge; retain separate coincident objects where one proprietary profile performs both functions.

preferred_term: compressed fibre-cement floor sheet, fibre-cement wall sheet or water-resistant plasterboard according to product and location
candidate_term: cement sheet, wet-area board, blueboard, villaboard or plasterboard
issue: These trade and product-family words do not identify a sheet's composition, thickness, edge, structural capacity or approved wet-area use. Floor substrates and wall linings also have different spans, fixings and joint systems.
next_action: Require verified product type, thickness, edge and manufacturer system before choosing substrate geometry, support spacing, fixings, joints or membrane treatment.

preferred_term: unenclosed shower and level-threshold shower as independent attributes
issue: Walk-in describes how a person enters, open usually describes enclosure, and hobless describes the absence of a raised kerb. A shower may be unenclosed but stepped, or enclosed with a level threshold, so none of these words determines the complete edge detail.
next_action: Ask separately about enclosure, kerb, level change, screen, opening and waterstop, then select the corresponding assembly parts and protection extents.

preferred_term: fire-resistant or fire-resisting for evidence-backed construction and fireproof only as informal search language
issue: Fire-rated is widely used but does not say whether the evidence applies to one product or a complete assembly, in which direction, for which criteria or under which test. Fireproof wrongly suggests unlimited protection.
next_action: Require the physical assembly, exposure direction, required criteria, tested or assessed result and evidence reference; retain fireproof only as a low-confidence search term.

preferred_term: fire-resistance level as performance metadata on a physical assembly
candidate_term: FRL as a wall, layer or product
issue: An FRL records structural adequacy, integrity and insulation results or requirements in a defined order. It is not a sheet, coating or generic material that can be drawn or transferred to a different build-up.
next_action: Store each required and achieved criterion, exposure direction, test or assessment reference and exact specimen assembly without creating an FRL geometry object.

preferred_term: fire-resisting separating wall when the wall separates the classified buildings or occupancies
candidate_term: party wall, intertenancy wall or dividing wall
issue: These common terms can refer to title boundaries, acoustic construction or walls in other NCC building classes. They do not establish the Class 1 or Class 10 relationship, fire path, rating, base-to-roof extent or service rules.
next_action: Ask which building classes and spaces the wall separates, then record the selected masonry or tested lightweight construction and its full junction extents.

preferred_term: fire-resisting external wall, separating wall or tested fire wall according to regulatory role
issue: A wall near an allotment boundary is not automatically fire-resisting, and the term fire wall has a more specific meaning in some NCC and commercial contexts. A dwelling separating wall follows another geometry and occupancy relationship.
next_action: Resolve boundary and building distances, building classes, wall exposure, wall start and roof termination before assigning a fire-wall family.

preferred_term: non-combustible for material classification and fire-resistant for assembly performance
issue: A non-combustible material does not burn under the applicable classification test, but an element made from it does not automatically achieve an FRL. Conversely, a tested fire-resistant lightweight assembly can contain combustible components.
next_action: Store combustibility on materials and fire resistance on exact assemblies as separate evidence fields; do not derive one from the other.

preferred_term: fire-resistant plasterboard or rigid fire-protection board according to product composition and system role
candidate_term: fire board, fire sheet or fire-rated plasterboard
issue: Fire board can mean gypsum plasterboard, calcium-silicate board, vermiculite board, coated penetration board or another proprietary product. None carries the complete wall, ceiling or encasement result by itself.
next_action: Require manufacturer, composition, product, thickness and tested-system position before drawing sheet layers, supports, joints or fixings.

preferred_term: roof-space separation lining, cavity barrier, fire block or firestop according to the path being closed
issue: These terms overlap in trade use. A roof-space lining is a plane, a cavity barrier closes a concealed void, a fire block may interrupt framing cavities, and a firestop protects a joint or service opening. Their hosts and geometry differ.
next_action: Identify the two spaces separated and whether the object is a planar lining, void closure, framing block, joint seal or penetration system before creating geometry.

preferred_term: passive firestop system for a tested opening or joint and high-temperature sealant for continuous service heat
candidate_term: fire caulk, fire sealant or high-temp sealant
issue: Firestop products are tested under a time-temperature fire exposure and may react chemically or expand. That does not make them suitable beside a continuously hot flue, appliance or pipe. Ordinary red sealant also has no automatic firestop performance.
next_action: Require the temperature regime, host, service, joint size, movement, product and tested application; never select a sealant from colour or the word fire alone.

preferred_term: intumescent fire collar, waterproofing collar, termite collar or roof penetration flashing according to protected hazard
issue: These components can all be rings around one pipe but control different hazards. A fire collar reacts to combustible-service loss, a waterproof collar seals a membrane, a termite collar blocks pest entry and a roof collar sheds weather.
next_action: Ask which barrier is penetrated and allow multiple coordinated collars on one service rather than promoting one collar to every protection role.

preferred_term: service-penetration opening for the void and firestop assembly for the complete protection
candidate_term: penetration, fire penetration or penetration seal
issue: Penetration can mean the service, the hole, the act of crossing or the finished protected system. Conflating them hides the host thickness, annular gaps, service supports, firestop products and evidence.
next_action: Model host opening, each penetrating service, residual gaps, supports, firestop parts and system evidence as linked records.

preferred_term: firestop control-joint or movement-joint system according to joint origin and movement
candidate_term: control joint, expansion joint, construction joint or fire joint
issue: These terms describe why a gap exists, not one universal fill. The firestop system must match the two host elements, joint width, direction, movement range, edge preparation and intersections.
next_action: Require the physical gap, hosts, movement and selected evidence before generating backing, fill, seal or cover layers.

preferred_term: self-closing solid-core protected-opening door or tested fire-resistant doorset according to the selected path
issue: Housing Provisions Part 9.2 includes a self-closing solid-core door alternative for certain external-wall openings. A tested fire-resistant doorset is a separately evidenced leaf, frame, hardware, seals and installation system. They cannot be silently exchanged.
next_action: Store the regulatory route, leaf and frame construction, closer, latch, seals, tag and evidence; never infer fire-door certification from a solid core.

preferred_term: non-openable fire-window assembly for the complete tested product and fire-resistant glazing for its pane
candidate_term: fire window, wired-glass window or fire glass
issue: Visible wire in glass does not establish the performance of the pane, frame, beads, seals, fixings or perimeter. Fire glass can also describe several different transparent products with different integrity, insulation and impact-safety evidence.
next_action: Require the complete tested opening system, pane make-up, support map, fixed operation, exposure direction, fire result and safety-glazing evidence.

preferred_term: domestic smoke alarm for the self-contained warning product and smoke detector for a detector connected to a separate control system
issue: A domestic alarm normally includes its sensor, sounder, power and controls. In larger systems a detector may only signal a separate panel and warning system. Using detector for both can omit the required local warning and power arrangement.
next_action: Ask whether the device contains its own sounder and household alarm functions or reports to a separate fire detection and alarm system.

preferred_term: photoelectric, ionisation or combined alarm according to certified sensing technology and jurisdiction
issue: AS 3786 covers more than one smoke-sensing principle, while state legislation and project requirements can mandate or favour a particular technology. Housing appearance does not reveal the sensor.
next_action: Store the product certification, sensing technology, jurisdiction, building date and replacement obligation instead of assigning a generic sensor from shape.

preferred_term: mains-powered for the power source and interconnected for the alarm-to-alarm warning relationship
issue: Hardwired often means mains powered but can also mean a dedicated interconnect conductor. Mains alarms may interconnect wirelessly, and battery alarms may be interconnected by radio or compatible wiring.
next_action: Record operating power, backup power and interconnect medium as three separate fields and verify device compatibility.

preferred_term: battery-powered alarm or mains alarm with backup battery according to operating power
candidate_term: battery alarm, lithium alarm or ten-year alarm
issue: A sealed lithium cell can be the only operating supply or a backup behind mains power. Ten-year is a product-life claim and does not identify sensing technology, interconnection, replacement rules or certification.
next_action: Store operating supply, backup supply, chemistry, replaceability, rated product life and replacement date independently.

preferred_term: smoke alarm or heat alarm according to detected fire product and permitted location
candidate_term: fire alarm or thermal smoke alarm
issue: A smoke alarm responds to airborne smoke using a certified chamber; a heat alarm responds to temperature. A heat alarm may be permitted or required in a specific garage situation but is not a universal substitute for dwelling smoke alarms.
next_action: Require the detected phenomenon, product standard, exact location, jurisdictional path and interconnection before choosing the device.

preferred_term: status indicator, visual alarm strobe or evacuation light according to function
candidate_term: alarm light, emergency light or flashing light
issue: A tiny status LED reports device state, a high-intensity strobe warns through vision, and an evacuation light illuminates a route. They differ in output, activation, coverage, power and accessibility purpose.
next_action: Ask whether the light communicates device state, warns occupants directly or illuminates an evacuation route, then model the correct coverage and power relationship.

preferred_term: firestop identification label, fire-door tag or heat-alarm notice according to the item and record purpose
candidate_term: fire tag, compliance label or notice
issue: All are durable markings, but a firestop label identifies one penetration system, a fire-door tag belongs to a doorset identity and a heat-alarm notice tells occupants about a garage interconnection arrangement.
next_action: Link each physical marking to the exact protected assembly, unique ID, evidence and maintenance record instead of using one generic compliance-label object.

preferred_term: thermal insulation product, bulk insulation, reflective insulation or thermal-mass element according to function
issue: Insulation slows heat flow, while thermal mass stores heat. Bulk and reflective insulation work differently and require different geometry, installation and evidence; they are not interchangeable labels for every thermally useful material.
next_action: Store product form, material, thermal function, tested rating and placement role separately; add thermal-mass elements in the relevant structural or lining catalogues.

preferred_term: material R-value or Total R-value according to the stated boundary
issue: A product or layer R-value is not the Total R-value of the complete roof, wall or floor. R-values are performance attributes, not drawable objects, and the result depends on the stated heat-flow direction and assembly path.
next_action: Require an R-value record to name the evaluated object or assembly, heat-flow direction, calculation or test basis, and whether bridging and surface films are included.

preferred_term: declared product R-value or installed assembly contribution according to evidence
candidate_term: installed R-value, rated R-value or effective R-value
issue: A declared laboratory value belongs to a product under stated conditions. Its installed contribution can be reduced by compression, gaps, moisture, settlement, discontinuity or thermal bridges, so one unqualified value can overstate the real assembly.
next_action: Keep declared, design and as-installed values separate and record thickness, compression, coverage, ageing or conditioning basis and evidence source.

preferred_term: insulation batt, blanket or roll according to supplied form
issue: These flexible products can use similar materials but have different supplied dimensions, facings, support needs and installation patterns. A roll cut into pieces does not automatically become a certified batt product.
next_action: Model the supplied product form separately from each cut or infill instance and retain parent-product evidence.

preferred_term: glass mineral wool or rock mineral wool according to fibre material
candidate_term: mineral wool, glass wool or rock wool
issue: Mineral wool is a family name that can include glass and rock fibres. The products may differ in density, fire, acoustic, handling and moisture properties even when their thermal role looks similar.
next_action: Use mineral wool only as a family classification; preserve the actual fibre type, density or grade and declared product evidence.

preferred_term: EPS, XPS, PIR, phenolic or other rigid insulation board according to material
candidate_term: foam board, polystyrene or rigid foam
issue: Expanded polystyrene, extruded polystyrene, polyisocyanurate and phenolic boards are distinct product families. They can differ in thermal ageing, moisture response, combustibility, facing, strength and compatible adhesives.
next_action: Require the polymer or foam family, facing, grade, thickness, edge profile and evidence instead of inferring properties from the generic board shape.

preferred_term: reflective insulation, roof sarking, wall wrap or reflective facing according to location and tested functions
issue: Foil describes a surface or laminate, not its complete role. A product may control water, air, vapour or radiant heat, but those functions require evidence and often depend on sealed laps and an adjacent airspace.
next_action: Store water, air, vapour and reflective classifications independently and model the required laps, seals, support and airspace.

preferred_term: vapour-control membrane classified by measured vapour permeance
candidate_term: vapour barrier, vapour check, vapour retarder or vapour-permeable membrane
issue: These names are often used loosely, while NCC placement depends on climate and the product's measured classification. Permeability is a spectrum; a membrane cannot be assigned a class from appearance alone.
next_action: Record measured permeance, classification, climate-zone rule, layer order, face orientation and product evidence.

preferred_term: vapour-permeable pliable membrane with stated classifications
candidate_term: breathable membrane or breathable house wrap
issue: Breathable is marketing shorthand and can be mistaken for deliberate airflow. Vapour diffusion through a membrane is not the same as an air leak, drained cavity or ventilation opening.
next_action: Avoid breathable as the stored class; record vapour permeance, air-barrier and water-control performance as separate properties.

preferred_term: air barrier, vapour-control layer and water-control layer according to tested role
issue: One physical membrane can perform several control functions, but those functions are not synonyms. A layer can resist bulk water yet remain vapour permeable, or control vapour without being the primary water barrier.
next_action: Allow one layer instance to carry multiple evidenced roles, while keeping each performance class and continuity network independently queryable.

preferred_term: primary insulation layer as an assembly role
candidate_term: main insulation, primary insulation or insulation line
issue: Primary insulation identifies the layer used as the reference for condensation and roof-space rules; it is not a product type. Different assemblies can assign the role to batts, boards, sprayed foam or another compliant layer.
next_action: Assign primary-insulation as a role within a specific assembly and never infer it solely from product category or thickness.

preferred_term: continuous insulation layer or thermal-break product according to extent and purpose
issue: Continuous insulation covers an area across repeating framing, while a thermal-break strip, pad or layer interrupts a specific conductive path. They can overlap in purpose but have different geometry and continuity requirements.
next_action: Record covered area, interrupted member path, thickness, material, joints and fastener penetrations rather than using one generic thermal-break flag.

preferred_term: thermal bridge as an assembly condition through identified physical members
candidate_term: thermal bridge object or cold bridge
issue: A thermal bridge is a heat-flow path caused by geometry or conductive materials, not an extra solid to draw. The framing, brackets, fasteners and gaps are objects; the bridge and its effect are analysis results.
next_action: Identify the physical path and mitigation objects, then store bridge fraction, psi-value or adjusted assembly result as analysis metadata.

preferred_term: reflective airspace, drained cavity or ventilated cavity according to function
issue: A clear airspace supporting reflective performance, a cavity draining water and a cavity carrying ventilation air are different void roles. One void may have multiple evidenced roles, but required thickness, openings and continuity differ.
next_action: Classify each void by role and record clear dimensions, bounding layers, obstructions, drainage or ventilation connections and evidence.

preferred_term: roof space, roof ventilation void or local ventilation gap according to bounded volume
issue: A whole roof space above a ceiling is not the same geometry as a narrow path above cathedral-roof insulation. Vent locations and free-area rules must connect to the actual volume being ventilated.
next_action: Model the exact bounded air volume and connect every inlet, outlet, baffle and obstruction to that volume.

preferred_term: vent opening, grille, louvre or screened terminal according to physical component, with net free open area as an attribute
issue: The gross face or hole size can be much larger than the net unobstructed airflow area after blades, mesh and framing are counted. Compliance calculations use free open area rather than a generic nominal size.
next_action: Draw actual openings and obstructions, store certified net free area separately, and aggregate only openings connected to the relevant ventilated volume.

preferred_term: rotary roof ventilator
candidate_term: whirlybird, turbine vent or roof fan
issue: Whirlybird is commonly used as a generic or brand-like term. A wind-driven rotary ventilator is not the same as a powered roof fan or static roof vent, and its capacity depends on operating conditions.
next_action: Store drive type, tested free area or capacity, base flashing, weathering and connected roof volume.

preferred_term: subfloor space beneath a suspended floor
issue: Underfloor can also mean the face of a floor assembly or services zone. A subfloor space is a bounded volume needing external air paths and cross-flow; it may be accessible or too shallow to crawl.
next_action: Use subfloor space for the bounded air volume and underfloor only as a placement direction or surface role.

preferred_term: subfloor brick vent, transfer opening or masonry weephole according to function
candidate_term: brick vent, air brick or weephole
issue: A subfloor vent supplies ventilation, an internal opening transfers air between subfloor compartments and a weephole drains or ventilates a masonry cavity. Their sizes, levels, screens and connected spaces differ.
next_action: Require every opening to name both connected spaces and its primary drainage, cavity or subfloor-ventilation function.

preferred_term: room exhaust fan or roof-space ventilator according to the air volume served
candidate_term: exhaust fan, roof fan or ventilation fan
issue: A bathroom or kitchen exhaust system removes indoor air to outdoors; a roof ventilator moves air from the roof space. Discharging a room fan into the roof space does not satisfy the outdoor-discharge path.
next_action: Connect the fan, duct and terminal to explicit source and destination volumes and reject room exhaust paths that terminate in a roof space.

preferred_term: ducted-to-outdoors rangehood or recirculating rangehood according to discharge path
issue: The visible appliance can look similar, but a recirculating unit filters and returns air indoors while a ducted unit carries it to an outdoor terminal. Their condensation-control effect and required components differ.
next_action: Record discharge mode explicitly and require a connected duct and outdoor terminal before classifying a rangehood as outdoor exhaust.

preferred_term: backdraft damper, fire damper, balancing damper or shut-off damper according to purpose
issue: A backdraft damper stops reverse airflow, a fire damper protects a fire separation, a balancing damper regulates flow and a shut-off damper closes an unused appliance path. Similar moving blades do not make the functions interchangeable.
next_action: Store damper purpose, normal position, actuator, leakage or fire rating, served path and access needs; add fire and balancing dampers in their specialist systems.

preferred_term: designed make-up-air opening or transfer path
candidate_term: make-up air, replacement air or natural leakage
issue: Make-up air is the replacement airflow required by exhaust, not a solid object. A defined opening, undercut or grille can provide a known path; accidental envelope leakage is uncontrolled and should not be represented as the same component.
next_action: Draw the physical opening and connected-space path, then store required and available airflow as analysis attributes.

preferred_term: door undercut for transfer air or door-bottom seal for air sealing according to design intent
issue: An undercut can intentionally transfer make-up air, while a sweep, drop seal or threshold seal closes leakage. Applying both requirements to the same door edge without coordination creates a direct design conflict.
next_action: Assign a door-bottom intent per room and verify that the selected transfer-air route and envelope or acoustic sealing requirements can coexist.

preferred_term: joint sealant, expanding-foam air seal, compressible strip or sprayed-foam insulation according to material and role
candidate_term: caulk, foam, spray foam or gap filler
issue: A bead sealant joins surfaces, expanding foam fills irregular gaps, a strip is compressed between components and sprayed foam can form an insulation layer. Products may not be interchangeable for movement, fire, UV, moisture or substrate compatibility.
next_action: Store product chemistry, joint or cavity geometry, movement, backing, exposure, fire and substrate constraints, and distinguish air-sealing use from insulation use.

preferred_term: stairway assembly, stair flight or individual step according to scope
issue: These everyday terms can mean the whole route between levels, one flight, or one step. A drawing tool must know whether landings, barriers, handrails and support structure are included.
next_action: Require the requested scope and level-to-level path, then generate flights, landings, steps and safety systems as related but separately editable objects.

preferred_term: physical tread, whole step or going dimension according to meaning
issue: The tread is the physical foot-supporting element, a step may include both tread and riser, and going is a measured horizontal distance between nosings. Going must not become another board in the model.
next_action: Draw tread and riser geometry; store going as a derived or specified dimension tied to successive nosing datums.

preferred_term: riser closure for the physical face and rise for the vertical dimension
issue: A riser can be a board or closed face, while rise is the vertical measurement from one tread level to the next. An open-riser stair has a rise dimension but no solid riser closure.
next_action: Represent the closure and the clear opening as physical alternatives, and keep rise as flight geometry.

preferred_term: stair flight for one uninterrupted series of steps
issue: Flight is a defined portion between landings. Run may mean the horizontal length, a ramp segment or an informal flight, so it is unsafe as the stored object name without context.
next_action: Segment level-to-level circulation at landings and give every stair flight its own step count, geometry, supports and adjacent barriers.

preferred_term: stair or ramp landing
issue: A landing is a level circulation area associated with a stair, ramp or doorway. It can be built like a small floor or deck, but its location and required clear geometry come from its circulation role.
next_action: Store both the physical deck/frame construction and the landing role, including connected flights, doors, barriers and clear circulation zone.

preferred_term: stair stringer, string or carriage according to supported system
candidate_term: stringer, string, carriage, cheek or stair beam
issue: Australian trade usage overlaps, while the physical geometry can be a cut timber string, housed string, steel plate, steel section or central spine. A skirt board may look similar but is lining, not the flight support.
next_action: Select the actual section and tread-support method; never infer structural support from a visible sloping trim board.

preferred_term: cut or open stringer for support geometry; open-riser stair for the step opening
issue: Open can describe a sawtooth stringer, the absence of riser closures, open sides without barriers, or a visually lightweight stair. These are independent conditions.
next_action: Ask separately for stringer form, riser closure and edge-barrier condition.

preferred_term: winder tread for a tapered tread changing stair direction
candidate_term: winder, kite step, tapered step or spiral step
issue: A winder is defined by plan taper and its role in changing direction. A spiral tread also tapers but belongs to a stair turning around a central axis, so the two need different generation rules.
next_action: Store walk-line geometry, narrow and wide ends, adjacent boundaries, centre or turning geometry and individual tread dimensions.

preferred_term: spiral stair, curved stair or geometric stair according to plan and support geometry
candidate_term: spiral, helical, circular or curved stair
issue: A spiral stair commonly winds around a centre post or small core; a helical or curved stair may have an open centre and different strings. The terms are often mixed in product descriptions.
next_action: Base the subtype on centreline, inner and outer support paths and tread geometry rather than the marketing name.

preferred_term: named support system with floating appearance as a visual attribute
issue: Floating describes appearance, not how loads are carried. The stair may use a central spine, hidden twin strings, wall-cantilevered treads or suspended connections, all requiring different physical objects.
next_action: Require the actual support and restraint scheme before generating a stair; keep floating only as a style or visibility tag.

preferred_term: building-serving pedestrian ramp
candidate_term: ramp, driveway, sloping path or threshold wedge
issue: These sloping surfaces serve different users, loads and code paths. A residential pedestrian ramp is not automatically a vehicle driveway or an accessible ramp complying with a separate accessibility standard.
next_action: Record route purpose, users, slope, crossfall, landings, edge treatment, surface, supporting construction and governing compliance path.

preferred_term: door threshold, threshold step or landing according to physical form
issue: A sill is usually part of a frame or weathering system, while a threshold may be a raised transition, a separate step assembly or a level landing at a door. Their clearances and weatherproofing interfaces differ.
next_action: Model each solid profile and level change, connect it to the doorway and landing, and keep door-frame weathering parts in the opening system.

preferred_term: slip-resistant surface with stated test classification and conditions
candidate_term: non-slip, anti-slip, safe grip or textured
issue: These informal descriptions do not prove performance. Surface material, finish, contamination, wear and whether it was tested wet or dry all affect the usable evidence.
next_action: Draw the actual finish or insert and attach test method, classification, test condition, substrate, direction, maintenance and evidence date as attributes.

preferred_term: pendulum classification or ramp-test classification as evidence metadata
candidate_term: P rating, R rating or slip rating
issue: P and R classifications arise from different test methods and are not physical layers or automatically interchangeable. A rating belongs to a tested product or surface configuration under stated conditions.
next_action: Store method, class, report, specimen construction and condition on the surface object; do not create rating geometry.

preferred_term: integral tread nosing, applied nosing assembly or tactile indicator according to object
candidate_term: nosing, stair strip, contrast strip or tactile strip
issue: The nosing can be the formed tread edge, a separately fixed carrier and insert, or a visual strip. Tactile ground-surface indicators are a different accessibility object and must not be generated from the word nosing.
next_action: Ask whether the edge is integral or applied and keep slip, luminance-contrast and tactile functions as separately evidenced roles.

preferred_term: fall-prevention barrier
candidate_term: barrier, balustrade, baluster, guard, guardrail or railing
issue: NCC language uses barrier for the complete fall-protection construction. Balustrade is common industry language, baluster is only one vertical member, and guardrail may also mean temporary site safety or road hardware.
next_action: Use barrier for the complete installed system and retain balustrade as a recognised industry alias; never map baluster to the whole assembly.

preferred_term: graspable handrail, barrier top rail or grabrail according to function
candidate_term: handrail, railing, top rail or grab rail
issue: A handrail is intended to be grasped for support while moving. A barrier top rail ties or caps the barrier and may not be graspable; a grabrail is normally a local accessibility or sanitary fitting.
next_action: Assign each rail its supported function, grasp profile, height datum, continuity, end treatment and structural connection; allow one designed rail to carry both evidenced roles.

preferred_term: barrier post, newel, baluster or picket according to role and size
candidate_term: post, newel, baluster, spindle, upright or picket
issue: Posts and newels are primary supports, while balusters and pickets are generally repeated infill members. A newel is associated with stair ends, landings or direction changes, not every vertical member.
next_action: Classify vertical members by support role, location, spacing and connected rails or panels rather than appearance alone.

preferred_term: solid barrier wall, framed infill panel, mesh or individual infill members according to construction
candidate_term: solid balustrade, panel, screen, wall or infill
issue: A structural wall or parapet can itself form a barrier, while a panel or mesh is normally supported infill within a separate frame. They need different quantities, connections, drainage and evidence.
next_action: Record whether the edge protection is a self-supporting wall or a framed infill system, then model its actual supports, joints and openings.

preferred_term: physical barrier objects with fall height, barrier height and opening limits as separate constraints
candidate_term: one-metre barrier, 125 gap or four-metre rule
issue: These numbers describe measurements and rule triggers, not objects. Fall height is measured at the hazard, barrier height from a specified datum, and opening limits apply to particular zones and configurations.
next_action: Draw barrier and openings explicitly, derive each datum from the relevant surface or nosing line, and evaluate the current rule set without naming geometry after a threshold value.

preferred_term: climbable-zone condition derived from barrier geometry
issue: Climbability is not a material or a hidden component. It depends on the arrangement of rails, wires, projections, openings and nearby footholds within the applicable hazard zone.
next_action: Preserve exact infill and rail geometry and calculate climbable features as a review result tied to the governing fall condition.

preferred_term: top-mounted or side-mounted barrier connection
candidate_term: face fix, fascia fix, side fix, deck mount or base mount
issue: These phrases overlap but refer to different host faces, edge distances, waterproofing penetrations and load paths. Fascia mount should not imply that a thin decorative fascia board is adequate structure.
next_action: Store the actual mounting face, backing structure, bracket or base plate, anchors, packers, edge distances and waterproofing interface.

preferred_term: stainless-steel wire rope in a tensioned barrier system
candidate_term: wire, cable, balustrade cable or stainless rope
issue: Cable may be mistaken for electrical or post-tensioning cable, and wire can mean a single strand. Barrier wire rope is a stranded structural infill component with a particular diameter, construction and termination system.
next_action: Record rope construction, diameter, grade, run direction, span, supports, terminal fittings, initial tension and inspection access.

preferred_term: wire tension as a state; tensioner, terminal and crimp as physical fittings
candidate_term: tension, tension fitting, swage, crimp or turnbuckle
issue: Tension is a force state, not hardware. A turnbuckle adjusts length, a swaged terminal is permanently formed onto rope, a swageless terminal grips mechanically, and a ferrule crimp forms a loop termination.
next_action: Draw every fitting at each rope end and change of direction, then store installed tension, adjustment range, lock-off and inspection state separately.

preferred_term: glass barrier with its actual spigots, channel, standoffs or clamps
issue: Frameless means the glass has little or no surrounding frame; it does not mean unsupported. Bases, anchors, holes, gaskets, clamps, joints and sometimes cap rails remain essential physical objects.
next_action: Require the support family and draw all glass-support and host-connection geometry even when the selected appearance is frameless.

preferred_term: structural glass barrier panel or framed infill glass panel according to load path
candidate_term: balustrade glass, structural glass or glass infill
issue: Glass directly spanning or cantilevering to resist barrier actions has a different role from glass infill supported on several edges within a post-and-rail frame. The required make-up and residual-risk strategy can differ.
next_action: Classify the panel from its support and load path, then store glass make-up, heat treatment, interlayer, holes, edges, supports and evidence.

preferred_term: spigot, glazing channel, clamp or standoff according to support geometry
candidate_term: glass fixing, bracket or frameless fitting
issue: These fittings support glass in different ways: bottom-edge point supports, continuous base restraint, local edge clamping or through-bolted stand-off restraint. They are not interchangeable symbols.
next_action: Choose the physical support family and preserve contact pads, holes, edge distances, anchors, adjustment and drainage.

preferred_term: glass-edge cap rail or offset glass-mounted handrail according to function and position
candidate_term: top rail, cap rail or handrail on glass
issue: A cap rail sits over and may connect glass top edges; an offset handrail is grasped and supported by brackets through or against the glass. One does not automatically satisfy the other role.
next_action: Record glass-edge restraint and graspable-support functions separately and draw the rail, bracket, holes, gaskets and end details actually selected.

preferred_term: window opening restrictor, protective screen or supplementary barrier according to mechanism
candidate_term: window guard, child-safe window, safety screen or rail
issue: A restrictor limits sash opening, a screen resists a person falling through the opening, and a rail forms a barrier in front. Insect screens and security screens are not automatically fall-protection systems.
next_action: Keep the opening-control, screen and barrier options distinct; link each to the actual sash, opening, host frame, fasteners and tested capacity.

preferred_term: building fall-prevention barrier or swimming-pool barrier according to hazard and governing path
candidate_term: safety fence, balustrade, pool fence or barrier
issue: A barrier at a deck edge and a swimming-pool barrier can look alike but respond to different hazards, access controls and referenced provisions. A compliant result for one role cannot be assumed for the other.
next_action: Keep pool barriers outside this slice and add their current NCC, state or territory and AS 1926 evidence in a dedicated specialist family.

preferred_term: building-serving stair or unrelated landscape steps according to route function
candidate_term: garden stairs, landscaping steps, entry steps or external stairs
issue: Housing Provisions stair rules apply to stairs serving the building in their stated scope, while unrelated landscaping can follow another approval and design path. Location outdoors alone does not decide the issue.
next_action: Record the route served, connected building entrances and approval context before assigning the Housing Provisions stair compliance path.

preferred_term: ordinary housing ramp or accessible ramp according to the selected compliance path
candidate_term: accessible ramp, wheelchair ramp, access ramp or pedestrian ramp
issue: A ramp under the general Housing Provisions is not automatically an accessible path designed to AS 1428.1. Accessibility brings additional geometry, handrail, kerb, landing and circulation requirements.
next_action: Store the governing path explicitly and add AS 1428.1 accessibility objects and constraints in a later licensed-standard review rather than silently applying them to every housing ramp.

preferred_term: livable housing
issue: Australian general usage often includes the extra e, but the NCC H8 title and ABCB Standard use livable. Search and user interfaces should recognise both spellings without producing two object families.
next_action: Use livable in canonical names and preserve liveable as a spelling alias for search and imported data.

preferred_term: NCC livable-housing feature, accessible design or adaptable design according to governing scope
candidate_term: livable, accessible, universal, adaptable or disability compliant
issue: These ideas overlap but are not equivalent compliance labels. H8 is a minimum housing pathway and the ABCB Standard expressly does not claim equivalence with AS 1428.1 or specialist accommodation requirements.
next_action: Store the nominated compliance pathway and never infer AS 1428.1 accessibility from an H8 object label alone.

preferred_term: step-free crossing with measured level difference and threshold profile
candidate_term: level, flush, flat, zero step or no threshold
issue: Step-free describes the usable crossing, while level and flush may describe only particular surfaces. A small bevel, drainage fall or permitted weathering profile can remain without the entrance being literally flat or having no physical sill.
next_action: Draw every finished surface and sill profile, then calculate the crossing condition from their actual levels and geometry.

preferred_term: H8 dwelling access path or AS 1428.1 continuous accessible path according to compliance path
candidate_term: accessible path, step-free path, wheelchair path or continuous path of travel
issue: An H8 route and a continuous accessible path can share physical paving and ramps but do not automatically share every width, gradient, landing, handrail, kerb or tactile requirement.
next_action: Keep the physical route reusable but attach each regulatory constraint set only when its governing path is selected.

preferred_term: path, ramp or step ramp according to physical form and gradient
candidate_term: sloping path, access ramp, step ramp or walkway
issue: These surfaces may join one route but have different geometry, allowable extents and supporting details. Calling every sloping surface a ramp loses the boundary between ordinary path fall and a distinct ramp segment.
next_action: Segment the route where gradient or construction changes and store each segment's physical surface, support, fall and regulatory role.

preferred_term: step ramp or doorway threshold ramp according to location and purpose
candidate_term: step ramp, threshold ramp, wedge or kerb ramp
issue: A step ramp replaces a small change of level along the access path, while a threshold ramp resolves a doorway sill profile. A kerb ramp is another accessibility and streetscape object; the labels should not silently merge.
next_action: Classify the object from its host and level change, then model its actual ramp surface, edges, junctions and drainage.

preferred_term: individual ramp segment plus aggregate ramp length as a calculated route value
candidate_term: maximum ramp length or total ramp
issue: A route can contain more than one separated ramp segment. The physical segments are objects; an aggregate limit is a rule calculation and must not be represented as one invented solid spanning intervening landings or paths.
next_action: Store segment lengths on physical ramps and compute any route-wide total from ordered route membership.

preferred_term: incorporated dwelling parking space
candidate_term: accessible parking bay, disabled bay, car space or hardstand
issue: The H8 parking origin serves the dwelling access route but is not automatically an AS 2890.6 accessible parking space with shared area, signs and pavement symbols. Hardstand names only a possible physical surface.
next_action: Record parking purpose, location, dimensions, surface, markings and selected standard without adding accessible-bay symbols or shared zones by assumption.

preferred_term: installed clear opening measured from the open door geometry
candidate_term: door width, leaf width, frame size, rough opening or clear opening
issue: These dimensions differ. Hinges, stops, handles, sliding-panel overlap and the actual open position can make the usable opening smaller than the leaf, frame or framed-wall opening.
next_action: Draw the installed frame, panel and hardware, store the fully open state, and derive clear opening between the actual obstructions.

preferred_term: nominated livable-housing entrance door
candidate_term: front door, main door, entry door or external door
issue: The H8 entrance is the selected door reached by the compliant access route; it need not be the door people casually call the front door. Other external doors do not inherit the role automatically.
next_action: Link one selected entrance to its access origin and route, while retaining architectural labels such as front, side or garage door separately.

preferred_term: entrance arrival landing, ramp landing or porch according to role
candidate_term: landing, entry platform, porch, stoop or doorstep
issue: An entrance arrival area provides manoeuvring and door operation space, a ramp landing interrupts or terminates a ramp, and a porch is a broader architectural assembly that may contain either. The same slab can carry more than one evidenced role.
next_action: Model the physical platform once and attach arrival, ramp and weather-cover roles with their separate datums and tests.

preferred_term: level entrance threshold, bevelled sill lip, ramped threshold or raised weather sill according to profile
candidate_term: flush sill, low sill, zero threshold, accessible threshold or weather sill
issue: Trade labels do not define the installed profile. Even a marketed flush or low sill can have tracks, lips, drainage slots and level differences that affect the crossing and weatherproofing.
next_action: Store a product-specific sill section with every ridge, rebate, track, drainage path and adjoining finished level.

preferred_term: coordinated step-free entrance weatherproofing system
candidate_term: remove the upstand, make the sill flush or add a strip drain
issue: Reducing the threshold height changes the water-control detail but does not remove the need for weatherproofing, drainage, flashing, termite inspection and sometimes bushfire coordination. A drain alone is not the whole system.
