next_action: Select and draw a complete water-control approach, including surface falls, sill, flashings, drain or drainage plane, outlets, cover and inspection interfaces.

preferred_term: finished clear corridor width
candidate_term: corridor width, framed width, wall-to-wall width or nominal hallway
issue: The usable width is between finished obstructions, not necessarily between stud centrelines or structural wall faces. Linings, skirtings, door hardware, radiators and fixed joinery can reduce it locally.
next_action: Derive corridor clearance from finished model faces and fixed projections along the selected route rather than from nominal framing dimensions.

preferred_term: sanitary compartment for the room and toilet pan for the fixture
candidate_term: toilet, WC, powder room, bathroom or sanitary facility
issue: Toilet can name the room or the ceramic fixture in everyday speech. The H8 room test needs a distinct enclosure object containing a distinct pan and any other fixed fixtures or door swings.
next_action: Use sanitary compartment for the selected room or space and toilet pan or suite for physical fixture records.

preferred_term: toilet-pan centreline and front-edge datums derived from fixture geometry
candidate_term: toilet centre, WC line, front clearance line or pan marker
issue: A centreline and front edge are geometric references, not additional building objects. Their positions change with the selected pan product and its installed transform.
next_action: Embed named datums in the parametric pan component and transform them with the installed fixture instead of drawing permanent construction lines.

preferred_term: sanitary-compartment circulation-space overlay
candidate_term: clear floor object, access zone, wheelchair box or empty slab
issue: Required circulation space is an absence-of-obstruction test over physical floor and around fixtures. Turning it into a solid creates false quantities, clashes and duplicate floor geometry.
next_action: Generate a non-quantity review overlay from the pan datums and test it against finished walls, fixtures, joinery, stops and relevant door positions.

preferred_term: hobless and step-free shower crossing as separately tested conditions
candidate_term: walk-in shower, level shower, hobless shower or accessible shower
issue: Hobless means there is no raised water-retaining hob; step-free means the crossing has no disqualifying level change. A marketed walk-in shower may still have a step, and neither label alone proves AS 1428.1 accessibility.
next_action: Store the shower entry profile, levels, waterstop and floor falls, then report hobless, step-free and accessibility results independently.

preferred_term: future-grabrail wall reinforcement
candidate_term: grabrail, grab rail, rail backing or accessible rail
issue: H8 Part 6 requires supporting construction for possible later attachment, not installation of the visible grabrail itself. Adding a rail by default changes the physical scope and can imply an accessibility design that has not been selected.
next_action: Generate concealed backing under H8 and reserve installed rail objects, profiles, clearances and fixings for a separately selected accessibility or fitout scope.

preferred_term: backing sheet, nogging, blocking member or metal plate according to physical form
candidate_term: backing, nogging, blocking, dwang, bracing or support
issue: Trades use these words loosely. Sheet backing forms a field, a nogging or blocking member spans framing, and a plate is a thin metal reinforcement; ordinary wall bracing or dwangs do not automatically occupy the correct future-rail zone.
next_action: Ask for material and geometry, then store fixture-relative extent, framing connection, fasteners and lining interface for the selected reinforcement form.

preferred_term: structural plywood grabrail backing with stated grade, thickness, support and fixing
candidate_term: ply, plywood lining, bathroom ply or timber sheet
issue: The presence of a plywood-looking layer does not establish structural capacity. Decorative lining, thin non-structural sheet or unsupported cabinet backing must not be treated as future-grabrail reinforcement.
next_action: Require structural product identity, thickness, edge support, stud support and fastening before assigning the backing role.

preferred_term: coordinated reinforced cavity-slider wall
candidate_term: cavity slider with backing, pocket wall or screw anywhere in the pocket
issue: A standard pocket contains a moving door panel and thin split studs. Future grabrail fasteners can strike or obstruct the panel unless a compatible reinforced build-up and safe fixing depth are deliberately designed.
next_action: Model the panel travel envelope, pocket framing, backing layer, fixing depth and exclusion zones together and require product or engineering confirmation.

preferred_term: qualified solid-wall future-grabrail substrate
candidate_term: masonry wall, concrete wall or no backing needed
issue: A suitable solid wall may provide inherent support, but hollow cores, chases, thin leaves, linings and services can prevent anchors from reaching adequate material. Material name alone does not prove the complete fixing path.
next_action: Reference the existing wall geometry and store solid thickness, voids, future anchor depth, edge distances, lining and evidence of capacity; do not add a fictitious backing layer.

preferred_term: H8 minimum provision or voluntary beyond-minimum feature according to selected scope
candidate_term: compliant, best practice, silver level, accessible or future proof
issue: Meeting the H8 minimum does not show that a dwelling meets a voluntary higher level, AS 1428.1 or every user's needs. Conversely, a project may deliberately add features beyond the minimum without changing the H8 object identity.
next_action: Store the claimed level and evidence source explicitly, report minimum and enhanced checks separately, and avoid marketing labels as compliance facts.

preferred_term: entrance drain channel, grate, outlet and sill drainage as separate objects
candidate_term: strip drain, channel drain, trench drain, slot drain or drained sill
issue: These terms can refer to the complete product or only its visible grate or slot. A door sill may also drain internally but is not the same object as an external landing channel.
next_action: Draw the body, trafficable top, outlet, end closures, waterproofing flange and sill drainage path selected by the product detail.

preferred_term: H8 applicability determined by current jurisdiction, adoption instrument and project date
candidate_term: nationally mandatory livable housing, NCC 2022 requirement or Australia-wide rule
issue: H8 appears in the national NCC text, but state and territory adoption dates and variations differ, and some jurisdictions disapply it. A national catalogue entry must not be treated as proof that H8 legally applies to every Australian project.
next_action: Ask for jurisdiction, approval pathway and relevant date, then load that jurisdiction's current adoption and variation rules before reporting compliance.

preferred_term: health-and-amenity physical system for the coordinated object set
candidate_term: H4 object, amenity item or compliance object
issue: H4 is a regulatory grouping, not one manufactured solid. It coordinates rooms, openings, facilities, wall assemblies and ceilings that also belong to architectural, structural and service systems.
next_action: Keep H4 as a coordination and checking layer over reusable physical objects rather than generating an H4-shaped solid or duplicating objects from other disciplines.

preferred_term: room height measured between nominated finished bounding surfaces
candidate_term: ceiling height, wall height, floor-to-floor height or storey height
issue: These dimensions can differ because floor finishes, ceiling linings, suspended construction, bulkheads and the structure above occupy real depth. A floor-to-floor dimension is not automatically the usable room height.
next_action: Derive room height from the actual finished floor and ceiling or underside faces at each tested point and retain other vertical dimensions separately.

preferred_term: finished ceiling face or underside of the relevant overhead construction
candidate_term: ceiling datum, underside, soffit, roof line or bottom chord
issue: The upper room-height boundary depends on what physically encloses the room. A visible lining, exposed structural underside, sloping roof lining, beam soffit and bulkhead are different surfaces and may produce different local results.
next_action: Let the user identify the governing overhead face where it cannot be inferred, and store that face reference with the room-height result.

preferred_term: sloping-ceiling compliant-area calculation over the physical room
candidate_term: low ceiling object, head-height volume or compliant ceiling solid
issue: A sloping room contains real floor, wall and ceiling geometry, but the portion satisfying a height rule is a calculated area or review overlay. Making it a material solid would create false quantities and clashes.
next_action: Intersect the room with the selected height plane for review and reporting, while keeping the result non-quantity-bearing.

preferred_term: habitable or non-habitable classification attached to a room or space
candidate_term: habitable object, living-area material or bedroom construction type
issue: Habitability describes use and regulatory treatment, not a distinct wall, floor or ceiling material. The same physical room may change nominated use without its enclosing objects being replaced.
next_action: Store room use and classification as project data and apply the relevant checks to the referenced enclosing construction.

preferred_term: natural-light opening, glazed area and light-transmitting area as distinct quantities
candidate_term: window area, glass area, daylight area or opening size
issue: Frame size, rough opening, visible glass and effective light-transmitting area are not interchangeable. Frames, mullions, opaque panels and lightwell geometry can reduce the daylight path.
next_action: Retain the physical opening and product geometry, then calculate each required area from the correct faces and product properties.

preferred_term: rooflight, roof window, tubular daylight device or lightwell according to physical form
candidate_term: skylight, rooflight, sun tunnel or roof window
issue: Skylight is used broadly in Australia, but an in-plane operable roof window, a kerbed rooflight and a small roof collector feeding a reflective tube have different construction and daylight paths. A lightwell is the shaft below a roof opening, not the rooflight itself.
next_action: Ask for product form and draw the roof penetration, weathering, glazing or collector, shaft and interior diffuser as separate applicable parts.

preferred_term: kitchen sink, washbasin and laundry washtub according to use
candidate_term: sink, basin, tub, trough or wash-up bowl
issue: Everyday and product language overlaps, but these fixtures serve different H4 facilities and usually have different bowls, heights, cabinetry, tapware and service arrangements.
next_action: Classify the fixture by its installed facility role and product data; preserve sink, basin, tub and trough as scoped search terms rather than universal synonyms.

preferred_term: food-preparation facility with a measured usable work surface
candidate_term: bench, benchtop, counter, island or kitchen cabinet
issue: The facility is the usable preparation arrangement, while a benchtop is one physical surface and cabinets are its support or storage. Appliances, sinks and upstands can interrupt the available work area.
next_action: Draw the complete joinery and fixtures, then derive usable preparation surface from unobstructed finished worktop faces.

preferred_term: kitchen cooktop or cooking hob, distinct from a shower hob
issue: In appliance language a hob is the cooking surface; in Australian wet-area construction a shower hob is a raised water-retaining curb. Searching or generating hob without context can select an entirely different building object.
next_action: Require kitchen or wet-area context and keep cooktop and shower-hob identifiers separate even when imported text uses hob alone.

preferred_term: freestanding cooker, built-in oven and built-in cooktop as separate appliance forms
candidate_term: stove, range, cooker, oven or cooktop
issue: Trade and consumer terms overlap. A freestanding cooker combines cooking surfaces and oven in one chassis, while built-in appliances require separate openings, support, restraints and clearances.
next_action: Select the appliance form before cutting cabinetry or floors and use manufacturer geometry for supports, anti-tip parts and installation interfaces.

preferred_term: washing-machine installation space and washing machine appliance as separate records
candidate_term: washer space, washing-machine provision or washing machine
issue: H4 can require space for an appliance without supplying the appliance itself. A clearance envelope has no material quantity, while the machine, hoses and guides are physical optional or project-supplied objects.
next_action: Store the required space as a non-quantity clearance and add product-specific appliance and connection objects only when selected or shown.

preferred_term: laundry washtub with nominated fixture and cabinet form
candidate_term: laundry tub, trough, sink, cabinet tub or wash trough
issue: These labels can describe a standalone trough, a tub bowl, or a combined stainless-steel tub-and-cabinet product. Treating them as one geometry loses supports, doors, rim seals and service space.
next_action: Represent the assembly, formed fixture and cabinet separately and retain product-specific capacity, openings, mounting and service connections.

preferred_term: waste fitting, overflow fitting and washing-machine rinse bypass as separate flow paths
candidate_term: drain, overflow, bypass, waste or hose connection
issue: The main waste drains the bowl, an overflow limits water level, and a rinse-bypass kit admits washing-machine discharge. Similar openings in a sink or tub do not perform the same function.
next_action: Draw and connect each actual opening and fitting by flow role, avoiding an invented generic drain connection that hides the route.

preferred_term: general sanitary facilities set, sanitary compartment and toilet suite as different scales
candidate_term: toilet, WC, bathroom, powder room or amenities
issue: The H4 facility set can include a closet pan and washbasin; the sanitary compartment is the enclosure; the suite is the installed pan and flushing components. Everyday toilet can mean any of the three.
next_action: Use explicit enclosure, facility-set and fixture records and attach colloquial room names only as scoped aliases.

preferred_term: outward-opening, sliding or externally removable sanitary door according to recovery method
candidate_term: compliant toilet door, emergency door or accessible door
issue: These are different physical ways of preventing an incapacitated occupant from trapping the door. The chosen swing, sliding hardware or external removal detail must be represented; the label compliant door is not geometry.
next_action: Record the selected recovery method and test the actual door movement, occupant location, frame, hinges and access to release or remove it.

preferred_term: external latch release and externally removable door as separate recovery provisions
candidate_term: emergency release, lift-off door or removable lock
issue: Releasing a privacy latch may unlock a door but does not remove an inward-swinging leaf blocked by an occupant. Lift-off hinges or removable pins affect the leaf-to-frame connection and perform another role.
next_action: Model latch release and leaf removal hardware independently and do not infer one from the presence of the other.

preferred_term: sound insulation between spaces, distinct from sound absorption within a space
candidate_term: acoustic treatment, soundproofing, acoustic insulation or noise control
issue: A separating wall reduces transmitted sound; absorptive finishes or cavity batts reduce reflections or resonances. A porous absorber alone is not a complete sound-insulating boundary.
next_action: Assign transmission performance to complete tested or assessed assemblies and absorption properties only to the applicable materials or surfaces.

preferred_term: Rw, Ctr and Rw plus Ctr as documented acoustic performance values
candidate_term: sound rating, acoustic thickness, dB wall or R-value
issue: These are standardised rating terms derived from evidence, not physical layers and not thermal R-values. Adding a thicker-looking board does not establish the result for the complete installed wall.
next_action: Store each rating with metric name, test or assessment, construction identity, standard edition and jurisdictional path; never generate a rating as geometry.

preferred_term: sound-insulating lining product within an evidenced complete wall system
candidate_term: acoustic plasterboard, sound-rated board or soundproof sheet
issue: A marketed acoustic board can contribute mass, but wall performance also depends on studs or leaves, cavities, insulation, fixings, joints, seals and services. The product label alone does not make the wall compliant.
next_action: Keep sheet identity and layer count explicit, but permit an assembly rating only when the whole build-up matches its evidence.

preferred_term: separating wall with stated buildings or occupancies separated
candidate_term: party wall, common wall, intertenancy wall, dividing wall or boundary wall
issue: These terms overlap in practice but can imply title boundaries, tenure, fire roles or other building classes. The H4 Class 1 sound path applies from the actual adjacency and jurisdiction, not the casual name alone.
next_action: Store the two spaces or buildings, classifications, association and boundary role explicitly and derive applicable acoustic and fire checks from them.

preferred_term: discontinuous construction only when the leaves are physically decoupled as required
candidate_term: double wall, twin wall, double-stud wall, staggered-stud wall or cavity wall
issue: Two visible leaves do not prove discontinuity. Shared studs, rigid ties, mortar droppings, noggings, services or another bridge can couple them, while staggered studs and double rows are not automatically equivalent details.
next_action: Generate each leaf and every connector, then test for prohibited rigid bridges and preserve the exact evidenced framing or masonry arrangement.

preferred_term: wall leaf for an independently supported side; lining layer for a sheet or finish on that leaf
candidate_term: skin, side, layer, panel, lining or leaf
issue: A leaf can contain masonry or framing plus several linings; a lining is only one layer. Counting every plasterboard sheet as a separate leaf misrepresents discontinuous construction and the load path.
next_action: Nest sheet and finish layers within their supported leaf and store physical separation and connections between leaves.

preferred_term: acoustic wall cavity and cavity insulation as separate objects
candidate_term: acoustic gap, insulated cavity, air space or acoustic insulation
issue: The cavity is the physical separation between leaves or linings; insulation occupies some or all of that space. The clear gap, insulation thickness and accidental bridges each affect the assembly differently.
next_action: Model cavity boundaries and installed insulation separately and expose clashes, debris or services that bridge the intended separation.

preferred_term: resilient tie, lining channel, isolation clip or pipe clip according to connection role
candidate_term: resilient mount, acoustic clip, furring channel, wall tie or rubber clip
issue: All reduce or control vibration transfer, but they connect different objects and carry different loads. Substituting one generic resilient component loses spacing, orientation, stiffness and supported construction.
next_action: Select a connection object from its two hosts and product evidence, then retain its section, spacing, fasteners and load direction.

preferred_term: direct transmission through the separating assembly and flanking transmission around it
candidate_term: sound leak, weak spot, bypass or acoustic gap
issue: Sound can cross the wall itself or travel through adjoining floors, roofs, ceilings, facades and services. Closing visible wall gaps does not address every flanking route, and flanking performance is not a material object.
next_action: Draw all boundary junctions and connected constructions, then report potential direct and flanking paths as graph-based review results.

preferred_term: joint compound, acoustic sealant and fire-resistant sealant according to physical joint and evidence
candidate_term: caulk, mud, gap filler, acoustic mastic or fire caulk
issue: Joint compound treats sheet joints, flexible acoustic sealant closes perimeter or service gaps, and a fire-resisting joint needs separate evidence. A product may satisfy more than one role, but the terms do not prove interchangeability.
next_action: Create the actual joint geometry and select material, backing, depth and evidence for every required acoustic, movement, weather or fire role.

preferred_term: acoustic service access panel with leaf, frame and perimeter seal
candidate_term: access hatch, inspection opening, removable panel or plasterboard patch
issue: A loose lining patch and a purpose-designed access assembly do not have the same repeatable fixing or seal. The opening can bypass the wall unless the complete panel construction preserves the evidenced performance.
next_action: Cut the real wall opening and generate the panel leaf, frame, fixings and seals from a documented system rather than drawing a symbolic rectangle.

preferred_term: acoustic pipe wrap, distinct from thermal insulation and condensation control
candidate_term: pipe lagging, insulation, wrap, blanket or soundproofing
issue: A wrap selected for noise control may differ in mass, facing, closure and continuity from thermal or condensation insulation. One product can have several evidenced roles, but appearance alone does not establish them.
next_action: Store wrap build-up, mass or acoustic evidence, seams, closure tape and pipe supports, and attach thermal properties only when separately known.

preferred_term: electrical outlet location and acoustic treatment as objects; outlet offset as a relationship
candidate_term: staggered outlets, offset GPOs, acoustic box or sealed power point
issue: The boxes, pads and caulk are physical; the separation between boxes on opposite wall faces is a measured relationship. Drawing an offset solid would duplicate geometry without preserving the two actual openings.
next_action: Generate each box and treatment in its host leaf and calculate opposed-box separation from their positions and penetrated layers.

preferred_term: national or Northern Territory Class 1 sound-insulation path selected explicitly
candidate_term: NCC acoustic wall, Australian party wall or standard H4 wall
issue: The Northern Territory has a specific Part 10.7 variation. A construction or rating accepted under one path must not be presented as the current rule everywhere in Australia.
next_action: Ask for jurisdiction and project pathway before selecting the construction table, rating target or compliance statement.

preferred_term: AS/NZS ISO 717.1:2004 for the cited NCC 2022 path and AS ISO 717.1:2024 as its published successor
candidate_term: current ISO 717, latest acoustic standard or AS 717.1
issue: A newer published edition does not silently replace the edition called up by an adopted NCC provision. Using an unspecified or latest edition can change the evidence basis and produce an unsupported compliance claim.
next_action: Store the exact standard identifier and edition on every rating result and update it only through an explicit adopted-code or project-specification decision.

preferred_term: H7 ancillary regulatory group and each physical assembly as separate concepts
candidate_term: H7 object, ancillary item or special construction
issue: H7 groups pools, alpine construction, heating appliances, bushfire construction and private shelters for regulation, but these do not form one physical object or one reusable tool.
next_action: Use H7 only as regulatory metadata and generate the selected pool, doorway, heating or bushfire assembly from its own object family.

preferred_term: AS 1926.1:2012 for NCC 2022 and AS 1926.1:2024 as its published successor
candidate_term: current pool-barrier standard, latest AS 1926 or AS 1926.1
issue: The 2024 publication and its 2025 supplement do not silently replace the 2012 edition called up by NCC 2022 Volume Two. An unspecified edition makes barrier evidence ambiguous.
next_action: Store the exact NCC edition, jurisdiction and standard edition on every pool-barrier check and product selection.

preferred_term: pool vessel, safety barrier and recirculation system as separate linked assemblies
candidate_term: pool, pool system or swimming-pool installation
issue: The water-retaining shell, child-access barrier and suction-safety equipment address different hazards. Treating them as one opaque component hides openings, gates, pipe networks and separate approval evidence.
next_action: Keep one coordinated pool project graph with independent vessel, barrier and hydraulic subassemblies and evidence.

preferred_term: pool safety barrier for access restriction and fall barrier for edge protection
candidate_term: fence, barrier, balustrade, railing or pool fence
issue: Both can use glass, posts and rails, but the child-access geometry, gate behaviour and surrounding climbable features differ from fall-protection requirements.
next_action: Assign explicit pool-access and fall-protection roles to shared hardware and require evidence for each role independently.

preferred_term: property boundary segment only when it is physically constructed and approved as part of the pool barrier
candidate_term: boundary, boundary fence, dividing fence or pool boundary
issue: A cadastral line is not a solid, and an ordinary dividing fence does not automatically satisfy the pool-barrier rules from both sides. Neighbour-side changes can also alter climbability.
next_action: Model the actual fence or wall faces, levels and adjoining features, then tag the segment's approved barrier role.

preferred_term: self-closing self-latching pool-gate assembly
candidate_term: garden gate, safety gate, fence gate or gate panel
issue: A pool gate is a system of leaf, supports, hinges, closer action, latch, striker, stop, opening direction and controlled gaps. A gate leaf alone does not provide the safety function.
next_action: Generate the full gate hardware graph and retain open, closing and latched states for inspection.

preferred_term: floating pool blanket, safety-rated pool cover and jurisdiction-permitted secure spa cover
candidate_term: pool cover, safety cover, blanket or spa lid
issue: These products can look similar but have different load, attachment and access-control roles. A normal floating blanket is not a child-resistant pool barrier.
next_action: Store cover type, product evidence and jurisdiction, and never infer a safety role from the word cover.

preferred_term: submerged pumped suction outlet
candidate_term: main drain, floor drain, pool drain or bottom drain
issue: The common main-drain label suggests a gravity waste outlet, but the object is commonly connected to pump suction and needs a matched sump, safety cover, fasteners and multi-outlet hydraulic design.
next_action: Use main drain only as a search alias and label the pipe connection as suction, gravity discharge or another verified service.

preferred_term: skimmer vacuum plate for cleaning and vacuum-release device for suction safety
candidate_term: vac plate, vacuum fitting, vacuum valve or vacuum release
issue: A vacuum plate intentionally applies pump suction to a cleaning hose; a vacuum-release device interrupts or relieves dangerous suction. Confusing them reverses their safety function.
next_action: Separate cleaning mode from blockage-safety controls in object selection, system state and user language.

preferred_term: suction pipe, return pipe and backwash-discharge pipe by hydraulic service
candidate_term: pool pipe, drain line, circulation line or waste line
issue: The three pipe services have different flow direction, pressure state, connection and discharge destination. One generic pipe route can create unsafe valves or unlawful discharge assumptions.
next_action: Require a hydraulic service on every pipe segment and validate permitted connections and flow direction.

preferred_term: waling plate for the Housing Provisions wall-attachment member
candidate_term: ledger, ledger board, ribbon board, bearer or wall plate
issue: Ledger is common international language, but bearer and wall plate already name different Australian framing roles. The Part 12.3 member has a specific wall-attachment function and limited application.
next_action: Use waling plate as the Australian canonical name, retain ledger as a search term and block this detail outside the Part 12.3 scope.

preferred_term: chemical bonded anchor or mechanical expansion anchor according to fixing mechanism
candidate_term: masonry anchor, dynabolt, chemset, bolt or fixing
issue: Bonded and mechanical anchors develop resistance differently and have distinct substrate, edge, hole-cleaning, orientation and installation requirements. Trade or proprietary names can hide the mechanism.
next_action: Select the anchor mechanism explicitly and require product capacity evidence for the actual filled-masonry substrate and orientation.

preferred_term: AS/NZS 2918:2018 for NCC 2022 and AS/NZS 2918:2026 as its published successor
candidate_term: current wood-heater standard, latest AS 2918 or AS/NZS 2918
issue: The 2026 successor does not silently replace the 2018 edition directly called up by NCC 2022 Housing Provisions. Mixing edition numbers breaks the evidence chain for appliance and flue installation.
next_action: Record the exact standard edition on every appliance and flue installation result and change it only through an explicit code or project decision.

preferred_term: open-fireplace front hearth and wood-heater floor protector according to appliance type
candidate_term: hearth, hearth pad, floor shield or non-combustible base
issue: Both protect the floor, but an open masonry fireplace hearth is part of a mass masonry assembly while a freestanding heater can use a tested layered floor protector with product-specific extent and thermal performance.
next_action: Choose the hearth object from the fire source and installation path, then generate its real layers and supported extent.

preferred_term: masonry chimney, active flue and outer flue casing as distinct objects
candidate_term: chimney, flue, flue pipe, chimney pipe or triple skin
issue: A masonry chimney is a loadbearing shaft; the active flue carries combustion gases; surrounding casings or insulation control surface temperature. Treating them as one pipe hides load and clearance relationships.
next_action: Generate each flue-system skin and annular space from one tested system and keep masonry chimneys as a separate structural assembly.

preferred_term: ventilated wall-shield assembly and clearance constraint
candidate_term: heat shield, fireproof sheet, clearance reducer or wall protector
issue: The sheet, spacers and open air path are physical; the allowed appliance separation is a result of the selected tested or prescribed construction. Drawing only a sheet does not create the shield performance.
next_action: Generate sheet, standoffs and open lower, upper and side air path, then evaluate appliance clearance separately.

preferred_term: bushfire attack level as project metadata and bushfire-resisting construction as physical objects
candidate_term: BAL wall, BAL material, BAL house or fireproof construction
issue: BAL describes assessed exposure, not a material. Complete walls, roofs, openings, decks and junctions respond to it through a selected pathway; no object becomes suitable merely by attaching a BAL label.
next_action: Store BAL and exposure inputs at project and element-evidence level while drawing the actual construction and junctions.

preferred_term: AS 3959 pathway or NASH NS300 pathway selected explicitly
candidate_term: NCC bushfire detail, steel-frame BAL detail or combined bushfire standard
issue: NCC Volume Two offers alternative construction paths. Picking the easiest provision from each can create a hybrid that neither standard supports.
next_action: Lock the project construction path before selecting bushfire details and keep all element evidence linked to that path.

preferred_term: ember-protection mesh with verified material and aperture
candidate_term: flyscreen, insect mesh, security mesh, spark mesh or BAL mesh
issue: Screens may differ in metal, aperture, frame, edge gaps, corrosion and tested role. A product described only as mesh cannot be assumed to restrict embers or resist radiant heat.
next_action: Store screen product, metal, aperture, open area, frame, edge seal and evidence; keep common mesh names as search aliases only.

preferred_term: gutter ember guard only when the complete roof-edge product has bushfire evidence
candidate_term: leaf guard, gutter mesh, gutter cover or ember guard
issue: A leaf guard can reduce debris but may use unsuitable combustible material, larger apertures or incomplete edge closures. Similar appearance does not establish ember protection.
next_action: Reuse the general gutter-guard geometry only after attaching verified bushfire material, aperture, edges, fixings and maintenance evidence.

preferred_term: Class 10c private bushfire shelter
candidate_term: bunker, cellar, safe room, fire refuge or underground room
issue: The trade word bunker and ordinary cellar language can imply safety without the H7P6 performance solution, tenability, access, structural and maintenance evidence required for a Class 10c shelter.
next_action: Use bunker and cellar only as search terms and require Class 10c classification and approved performance-solution evidence before any safety claim.

preferred_term: private bushfire-shelter performance-solution object library, not a compliant template
candidate_term: standard bushfire bunker, approved shelter design or NCC shelter kit
issue: NCC Volume Two and the Housing Provisions contain no Deemed-to-Satisfy path for H7P6, and the ABCB performance standard is not a prescriptive acceptable design.
next_action: Limit future tools to documenting engineer-selected parts, inputs and evidence; never offer a one-click compliant shelter.

preferred_term: engineered bushfire-shelter protective door or hatch
candidate_term: fire door, bunker door, steel door or cellar hatch
issue: A conventional building fire-door rating or steel plate does not prove resistance to the shelter's combined thermal, pressure, debris, leakage and emergency-operability conditions.
next_action: Treat leaf, frame, latches, seals, opening direction and internal release as one engineered system with event-specific evidence.

preferred_term: occupant capacity, maximum occupancy period and tenability results as approved metadata
candidate_term: number of seats, room area, safe duration or bunker capacity
issue: Floor area and seats alone do not establish breathable air, temperature, humidity, carbon-dioxide, smoke or egress conditions. The values are results of the complete performance design.
next_action: Import approved capacity, duration and tenability evidence and display it on the internal sign without calculating it from geometry alone.

preferred_term: cold-water service and drinking-water service according to temperature and permitted use
candidate_term: cold water, mains water, potable water or drinking water
issue: Cold describes a service that is not intentionally heated; drinking describes approved use and water-contact requirements. Rainwater or another alternative source can sometimes supply either category, so the terms are not interchangeable.
next_action: Store source, intended use and service temperature separately, then select products and outlets from all three fields.

preferred_term: non-drinking-water service and rainwater service as separate NCC service families
candidate_term: non-potable, recycled, alternative, tank or rain water
issue: NCC Volume Three treats non-drinking water under Part B3 and rainwater services under Part B6. A rainwater pipe may serve approved drinking uses in some projects, while recycled water is not automatically rainwater.
next_action: Require an explicit source and permitted-use selection instead of inferring safety from pipe colour or the word tank.

preferred_term: sanitary plumbing upstream and sanitary drainage downstream of the defined connection boundary
candidate_term: waste pipe, sewer pipe, house drain or DWV system
issue: Sanitary plumbing and sanitary drainage can use similar pipes but have different regulatory extents, layout rules, supports, access and burial conditions. One continuous model run still needs a recorded boundary node.
next_action: Create an explicit plumbing-to-drainage connection object or node when a future route crosses the regulatory boundary.

preferred_term: heated-water service upstream and tempered-water service downstream of a temperature-control device
candidate_term: hot water, warm water, tempered water or hot-water line
issue: A stored or distributed heated-water circuit can be hotter than water delivered at selected personal-hygiene outlets. Tempered water describes the controlled downstream branch, not the complete heater circuit.
next_action: Split the route at the actual mixing or limiting device and tag only its controlled outlet branches as tempered.

preferred_term: water heater for the appliance and heated-water service for the complete connected system
candidate_term: hot-water system, HWS, cylinder, tank or heater
issue: Calling the whole system a heater hides inlet controls, relief paths, temperature control, circulation, pipe insulation and drainage. Calling a storage vessel a complete system hides its heat source and valves.
next_action: Generate the appliance, connected valves, relief drains and distribution as separate selectable objects within one system assembly.

preferred_term: pressure-reducing valve and pressure-relief valve according to flow function
issue: PRV is used for two very different devices: one throttles downstream supply pressure, while the other opens to discharge excessive pressure. Substituting one for the other creates a dangerous hydraulic model.
next_action: Do not accept PRV as a final selection; ask whether the device controls supply pressure or discharges excess pressure.

preferred_term: check valve, dual-check valve and double-check-valve assembly as distinct devices
candidate_term: non-return valve, check, dual check, double check or DCV
issue: The names can sound equivalent but differ in element count, testability, isolation, certification and permitted backflow-protection role. A generic flap symbol cannot establish the assembly type.
next_action: Store full certified device designation, testability and selected protection role instead of normalising every item to check valve.

preferred_term: reduced-pressure-zone backflow device
candidate_term: RPZD, RPZ valve, pressure reducer or pressure-zone valve
issue: An RPZD is a testable backflow-protection assembly with checks and an intermediate relief zone. It is not a pressure-reducing supply valve despite similar initials and words.
next_action: Keep RPZD search aliases tied only to the backflow assembly and reserve pressure reducer for downstream-pressure control.

preferred_term: air gap, air break and tundish according to the physical separation and visibility required
candidate_term: open drain, indirect waste, break, gap or tundish
issue: An air gap is an unobstructed vertical separation, an air break is a different indirect connection arrangement, and a tundish is a receiving fitting that can make discharge visible. Similar open geometry does not make them interchangeable.
next_action: Generate the named separation and its spill, overflow and drainage envelope from the selected connection purpose.

preferred_term: water-heater relief drain and safe-tray drain as separate discharge paths
candidate_term: overflow pipe, relief pipe, drain line or tray pipe
issue: A relief drain carries deliberate valve discharge; a safe-tray drain carries leakage collected around the appliance. Combining them can hide a leaking heater, obstruct relief flow or defeat visible discharge.
next_action: Route each path from its actual source to its approved termination and preserve visible outlets where required.

preferred_term: rainwater storage system, rainwater service and alternative drinking-water service according to role
candidate_term: tank water, rainwater system, rainwater harvesting or private supply
issue: The tank is storage, the rainwater service distributes stored roof water, and an approved alternative drinking-water path includes source treatment and drinking-water product requirements. Tank water alone establishes none of those uses.
next_action: Ask separately for storage role, water source, treatment and every permitted outlet use.

preferred_term: rainwater reuse tank, stormwater detention tank and combined tank with explicit compartment or outlet roles
candidate_term: stormwater tank, rain tank, detention tank or retention tank
issue: Reuse storage holds water for a service; detention storage temporarily controls discharge; retention can mean different things locally. One vessel can combine roles only when its levels, outlets and reserved volumes are explicit.
next_action: Represent each storage volume, inlet and outlet role instead of choosing the tank type from its external shape.

preferred_term: sanitary stack, vent stack and stack vent as three distinct pipe roles
candidate_term: soil stack, waste stack, main vent or vented stack
issue: A sanitary stack carries discharge; a vent stack is a separate vent-only riser; a stack vent is the continuation of a discharge stack above its highest connection. Reversed word order changes the object.
next_action: Store the discharge or vent role along every pipe segment and split it where the stack becomes its vent continuation.

preferred_term: drain, waste and vent as service roles rather than a single pipe identity
candidate_term: DWV pipe, sewer pipe, PVC waste or vent pipe
issue: One product family can be installed as a fixture waste, graded drain or air vent. The route, grade, connection rules and contents come from the assigned role, not from the letters DWV on the pipe.
next_action: Make service role mandatory for each DWV run and use material or product series as a separate selection.

preferred_term: floor waste within the floor assembly and gully within sanitary drainage
candidate_term: floor drain, waste, gully, grate or trap
issue: A floor waste receives surface or fixture discharge inside a floor system; an external drainage gully is a trapped drainage node with different level, overflow, surround and connection roles.
next_action: Choose from host and function: wet-area floor assembly, external disconnector, or surcharge relief point.

preferred_term: overflow relief gully for the deliberate external surcharge-relief point
candidate_term: ORG, overflow, gully, floor waste or sewer relief
issue: The ORG function depends on its grate elevation relative to fixtures and a clear external overflow route. A trapped grate that looks identical can be only a disconnector gully and a floor waste cannot automatically replace it.
next_action: Calculate and display the level relationship and keep the relief grate and surrounding flow path unobstructed.

preferred_term: boundary trap for air separation and backwater valve for reverse-flow closure
candidate_term: reflux trap, sewer trap, non-return valve or boundary valve
issue: A boundary trap maintains a water seal between property and sewer air spaces; a backwater valve closes mechanically under reverse flow. They solve different problems and have different maintenance consequences.
next_action: Ask whether the design needs air disconnection, surcharge protection or both, then retain authority requirements as metadata.

preferred_term: septic tank for the primary-treatment vessel and onsite wastewater system for the complete property arrangement
candidate_term: septic system, septic, treatment tank or disposal system
issue: A septic tank only settles and stores solids. The complete system also needs inlet drainage, downstream treatment where selected, dosing, land application, access and ongoing servicing.
next_action: Treat septic tank selection as one node in the full source-to-soil hydraulic path.

preferred_term: secondary treatment system as the broad class and AWTS only for an aerated system
candidate_term: STS, AWTS, aerobic system, treatment plant or bio system
issue: Secondary treatment can use several technologies; AWTS specifically relies on supplied aeration and has characteristic blowers, diffusers and controls. Using AWTS for every plant invents physical components.
next_action: Select the certified process family before instantiating aeration, media, clarification or disinfection components.

preferred_term: greywater from selected bath, shower, basin and laundry sources; blackwater or sewage for toilet and contaminated wastewater
candidate_term: wastewater, sullage, recycled water, grey water or household waste
issue: Source classification controls whether diversion or treatment equipment is permitted. Greywater is not already recycled water, and kitchen or toilet discharges cannot be assigned by pipe colour alone.
next_action: Require every diverted branch to identify its source fixtures and keep a fail-safe sanitary-drainage path.

preferred_term: effluent absorption trench with its pipe, aggregate or arch, separator and soil cover
candidate_term: leach drain, soakage trench, absorption bed, septic trench or rubble drain
issue: The legacy names can hide whether the system is for wastewater or stormwater and whether it uses aggregate, chambers, pressure distribution or gravity. The physical layers and approved effluent class must be explicit.
next_action: Generate the trench type and every material layer, then keep soil loading and setback approval as linked metadata.

preferred_term: treatment capacity, effluent quality, hazard rating and hydraulic duty as evidence metadata
candidate_term: compliant tank, high-hazard valve, treatment-volume solid or certified pump shape
issue: Capacities and performance classifications are not extra physical solids. They result from selected products, complete systems, operating assumptions, approvals and testing, and cannot be inferred from approximate SketchUp volume.
next_action: Draw the selected physical carrier and import its certified performance, duty and approval values without calculating compliance from geometry.

preferred_term: AS/NZS 3500:2021 series for the NCC 2022 national call-up and the 2025 series only where adopted or selected explicitly
candidate_term: current plumbing standard, latest AS 3500 or AS/NZS 3500
issue: The 2025 editions are published successors but do not silently replace the 2021 editions called up nationally by NCC 2022 Amendment 2. Jurisdictions can adopt the new series on different dates and with variations.
next_action: Store jurisdiction, approval date, code pathway and exact standard edition on every generated hydraulic design.

preferred_term: WaterMark and Lead Free WaterMark as product-evidence fields
candidate_term: WaterMarked object, lead-free geometry, certified valve or approved pipe
issue: The marks are evidence attached to selected products; they are not separate building objects and cannot be proven by appearance. Lead-free requirements apply to relevant copper-alloy products conveying drinking water from 1 May 2026.
next_action: Attach certification identifiers, scope and lead-free evidence to product instances while keeping geometry generic until a product is selected.

preferred_term: electrical installation for the fixed connected system and fixed equipment for a selected connected item
candidate_term: electrics, wiring, appliance or electrical object
issue: An electrical installation is the coordinated fixed system, not one cable or appliance. A portable appliance is generally outside the building-member ontology unless its installed connection or spatial interface is being modelled.
next_action: Require tools to choose system, fixed equipment, connection assembly or portable product scope explicitly.

preferred_term: consumer mains, submain and final subcircuit as distinct circuit roles
candidate_term: mains cable, feed, circuit or house wire
issue: The three terms describe different positions in the distribution tree. Treating every feeder as a final circuit loses switchboard boundaries, ownership, protection and cable-sizing context.
next_action: Generate the distribution tree first, then assign each cable run its exact circuit role and endpoints.

preferred_term: network service line on the distributor side and consumer mains on the installation side
issue: The physical ownership and boundary can change by network and jurisdiction. The two cable paths must not be merged simply because both bring supply toward the meter or switchboard.
next_action: Store distributor, network boundary, ownership and actual endpoints on every service instance.

preferred_term: meter enclosure, switchboard and electricity meter as separate objects
candidate_term: meter box, fuse box, power box or board
issue: A common cabinet can contain metering and switchboard sections, but the enclosure, panel, revenue meter and switching equipment are different replaceable and owned parts.
next_action: Allow one combined cabinet while retaining distinct containment, metering and switchboard components.

preferred_term: RCD as the protective function, with RCCB, RCBO and MCB kept as distinct device types
candidate_term: safety switch, breaker or RCD breaker
issue: RCCBs provide residual-current protection without integral overcurrent protection; RCBOs combine both; MCBs provide overcurrent protection but are not RCDs. Trade language often hides the difference.
next_action: Require protective functions and device construction as separate attributes before selecting geometry.

preferred_term: MEN link, neutral link and earth bar as separate switchboard connectors
candidate_term: earth link, neutral bar or grounding bar
issue: These conductors and terminal bars have different roles even when mounted close together. Merging them can create an electrically impossible switchboard model.
next_action: Generate each bar or link from the selected earthing arrangement and keep its connected conductors explicit.

preferred_term: socket-outlet installation for the whole installed point and socket mechanism for the contact component
candidate_term: power point, GPO, outlet, socket or plug point
issue: Australian trade terms can refer to the visible plate, one socket mechanism or the complete installed point. A drawing tool must know whether it is placing the assembly, plate, mechanism, box or circuit.
next_action: Use the complete installation as the placement tool and expose mechanisms, plate and box as editable parts.

preferred_term: switch for normal control and isolator or switch-disconnector for the documented isolation function
candidate_term: switch, shut-off, isolation switch or disconnect
issue: A wall switch, circuit breaker, main switch and local isolator are not interchangeable even when each has an on-off handle.
next_action: Store control, protection and isolation functions before assigning device families or symbols.

preferred_term: junction box for cable connections and mounting box or bracket for an accessory support
candidate_term: electrical box, wall box, J-box or adaptable box
issue: Boxes can look similar but have different openings, covers, loads and access needs. A box behind a power point is not automatically a junction box.
next_action: Select boxes from their role, host, cover and service-access requirements rather than outline alone.

preferred_term: cable as conductor assembly, conduit as closed pathway and trunking or tray as separate containment systems
candidate_term: wire, pipe, duct, raceway or cable tray
issue: The terms describe different physical layers. Treating the cable centreline as conduit geometry loses fill, bends, fittings, supports and access covers.
next_action: Route cables and containment as linked but independently drawable runs with separate fittings and supports.

preferred_term: low voltage and extra-low voltage as electrical classifications, not casual descriptions
candidate_term: low-voltage cable, data voltage, mains voltage or safe voltage
issue: In everyday speech 230 V is called high voltage, but Australian electrical classifications use technical boundaries. Communications and control circuits also need their actual separation and power source recorded.
next_action: Use the exact current standard definitions in rule evaluation and keep friendly UI wording separate from electrical classification.

preferred_term: lighting point, luminaire and lamp as separate levels
candidate_term: light, light fitting, globe or fixture
issue: A lighting point is the installed connection and support location; the luminaire is the complete fitting; a replaceable lamp is only its light source. Integrated LED fittings may have no replaceable lamp.
next_action: Let tools place a lighting point and then select luminaire construction and light-source anatomy.

preferred_term: selected downlight product, optional physical guard and documented clearance or insulation-contact evidence
candidate_term: IC-rated object, downlight clearance box, heat shield or fire hood
issue: An IC classification and clearance requirement are product evidence, not automatic solid geometry. A guard is a real optional product and must not be invented around every downlight.
next_action: Import classification and clearance metadata from the selected luminaire and generate a guard only when the documented arrangement includes one.

preferred_term: lighting power density and control compliance as analysis results
candidate_term: NCC light object, compliant lighting zone or wattage solid
issue: Housing Provisions 13.7.6 regulates artificial-lighting energy through a calculation and controls, with a NSW deletion. The power-density limit is not a physical component.
next_action: Draw luminaires and controls, then evaluate jurisdiction-specific energy rules from schedules and spaces.

preferred_term: PCD or utility box, NTD or connection box, and router or gateway as distinct network layers
candidate_term: nbn box, modem, connection box or router
issue: The external premises connection device, carrier network termination equipment and customer router have different ownership, cabling and power needs. Their forms also vary by access technology.
next_action: Ask for access technology and installed equipment, then model carrier-owned and customer-owned layers separately.

preferred_term: data outlet, telephone outlet and coaxial television outlet as separate connector systems
candidate_term: communications point, network point, phone point or TV point
issue: Similar faceplates can hold electrically and mechanically incompatible mechanisms. The visible plate cannot determine the service or cable behind it.
next_action: Store connector, cable medium, category or frequency role and tested service for every communications outlet.

preferred_term: photovoltaic module for electricity generation and solar thermal collector for heat
issue: Solar panel is common but ambiguous. PV modules contain cells and electrical leads; solar hot-water collectors contain fluid or heat-transfer paths and belong to a different system.
next_action: Ask whether the object generates electricity or heat before selecting its catalogue family.

preferred_term: PV module, string and array as distinct nested assemblies
candidate_term: panel string, solar bank, row or array
issue: A string is a series electrical circuit and can cross geometric rows; an array is the broader connected generating group. Visual row geometry alone cannot establish string topology.
next_action: Keep module placement, racking rows and electrical string membership as linked but independent data.

preferred_term: string inverter, microinverter, DC optimiser, battery inverter and hybrid inverter as separate device types
candidate_term: solar inverter, converter, optimiser or battery charger
issue: The devices occupy different locations and have different DC, AC and battery connections. A hybrid inverter is not simply a string inverter with an assumed battery added.
next_action: Select architecture before generating converter quantity, location, cabling and isolation.

preferred_term: BESS for the complete installed system, battery unit for the product and battery module for an internal block
candidate_term: battery, home battery, battery pack or solar battery
issue: The complete system also includes power conversion, controls, protection and sometimes backup switching. A module is not a safe stand-alone installation object.
next_action: Place the system assembly, then expose product units, modules and supporting equipment only where that architecture uses them.

preferred_term: documented PV DC isolation or disconnection device at its actual location
issue: AS/NZS 5033:2021 changed the former blanket rooftop-isolator approach. Some designs use other disconnection arrangements, and a generic tool must not insert a roof switch by default.
next_action: Generate only the isolation architecture documented for the project, inverter and jurisdiction.

preferred_term: EVSE for fixed supply equipment and onboard charger for vehicle conversion equipment
candidate_term: EV charger, wallbox, charging point or car charger
issue: The fixed wall or pedestal unit controls and supplies the connection, while the vehicle commonly contains the onboard AC charger. Everyday language calls both the charger.
next_action: Use friendly UI wording but store EVSE form, mode, connector, circuit and vehicle interface explicitly.

preferred_term: RCM, EESS registration and product certification as evidence fields
candidate_term: RCM object, certified charger, approved light or compliant appliance geometry
issue: Marks and registrations concern selected equipment and suppliers. They are not separate building solids and cannot be proven from a generic model shape.
next_action: Attach evidence identifiers, responsible supplier and scope to product instances without claiming certification from appearance.

preferred_term: exact electrical standard edition, amendment state, jurisdiction and adoption date
candidate_term: current Australian Standard, latest Wiring Rules or compliant to AS/NZS
issue: Publication and legal adoption are different. AS/NZS 3008.1.1:2025 and AS/NZS 3112:2025 illustrate edition transitions, while state rules and network documents can apply on different dates.
next_action: Persist standard designation, edition, amendments, jurisdictional instrument and project approval date on every rule result.

preferred_term: clearances, ratings, calculations, network approval and test results as linked evidence or analysis
candidate_term: clearance solid, certified volume, compliant cable size or approved equipment shape
issue: These values depend on selected products, circuits, environment, jurisdiction and verification. Approximate SketchUp geometry cannot establish them by itself.
next_action: Draw physical carriers and optionally display non-solid analysis overlays, while keeping compliance claims evidence-backed.

preferred_term: optional or legacy backup hardware only when selected or found in the existing installation
candidate_term: every nbn connection has battery backup or every home battery backs up the house
issue: nbn stopped supplying new battery-backup units in June 2024, and BESS backup needs specific transfer equipment and load architecture. Neither backup path is universal.
next_action: Ask whether backup is installed, what equipment performs it and which loads are supplied before drawing the arrangement.

preferred_term: camera view, detector coverage and wireless coverage as analysis fields linked to physical devices
candidate_term: camera cone object, alarm coverage solid or Wi-Fi room object
issue: The visible volume can be useful as an overlay, but it is not a building material and does not prove performance. Furniture, heat sources, radio attenuation, privacy and commissioning can change the result.
next_action: Offer optional analysis overlays and store assumptions, but exclude them from physical material quantities.

preferred_term: physical test tag linked to an inspection record
candidate_term: tested object, safe tag or compliant lead
issue: A tag is a physical label and historical record pointer. It does not itself prove present condition, correct test method or continuing safety.
next_action: Model the tag only where needed and keep inspection date, method, result and inspector as separately verifiable evidence.

preferred_term: single-split, multi-split or ducted reverse-cycle system according to the actual topology
candidate_term: split system or reverse-cycle system as one interchangeable object
issue: A single split has one indoor and one outdoor unit. A multi-split branches one outdoor unit to several indoor units. A ducted system uses a central fan coil and an air-distribution network. They can share refrigeration principles without sharing drawable parts or connection patterns.
next_action: Ask for the equipment and connection topology before generating indoor units, branches or ducts.

preferred_term: outdoor unit for the complete reversible product and outdoor heat exchanger for the coil
issue: Condenser is common trade language, but a reverse-cycle outdoor coil rejects heat in cooling and absorbs heat in heating. Calling the whole assembly a condenser can also hide its compressor, fan, valves, casing and controls.
next_action: Accept condenser as search language but preserve complete-unit identity and current operating mode separately.

preferred_term: indoor heat exchanger or indoor unit according to the physical scope
issue: The indoor coil evaporates refrigerant in cooling but can condense it in reverse-cycle heating. The indoor unit also contains a fan, filter, drain pan, casing and controls, so coil and unit are not synonyms.
next_action: Store coil role by operating mode and never substitute the internal coil for the complete indoor equipment object.

preferred_term: refrigerant fan-coil unit or hydronic fan-coil unit with the energy-transfer circuit stated
issue: Fan coil describes air moved over a coil, but the coil may contain direct-expansion refrigerant or heating and cooling water. Identical-looking casings can require completely different pipework, valves, safety data and controls.
next_action: Require the connected fluid and system type before selecting fittings, drains, valves or licences.

preferred_term: refrigerant gas line and refrigerant liquid line for the tubes, paired refrigerant lines for the pair and service bundle for all grouped services
candidate_term: pair coil, line set, pipe pair or AC bundle
issue: Trade terms can mean two insulated copper tubes, a factory twin tube product, or the whole capping route containing tubes, drain and cable. Gas and liquid are circuit roles and actual refrigerant phase varies with mode and location.
next_action: Model each tube, its insulation and the optional capping or service bundle as separate nested objects.

preferred_term: HRV when heat transfer is established and ERV only when moisture or enthalpy transfer is established
candidate_term: HRV, ERV, heat recovery and energy recovery as automatic synonyms
issue: Both systems can have four ducts, two fans and a core. Moisture transfer depends on the selected core and declared product performance, not its box shape or the presence of heat recovery.
next_action: Store sensible and latent transfer evidence independently and do not infer ERV behaviour from generic core geometry.

preferred_term: grille, register and diffuser as distinct terminal forms
candidate_term: vent, grille, register, diffuser or outlet
issue: Everyday usage merges these terms. A grille is primarily an open-faced terminal, a register commonly adds an integral damper, and a diffuser is shaped to distribute supply air in a designed pattern. Return grilles and supply diffusers also have different air-path roles.
next_action: Use vent for friendly search only; require terminal role, face form, neck, integral damper and airflow pattern for generation.

preferred_term: multi-directional outlet with the actual face and neck geometry stored
issue: MDO is common Australian HVAC shorthand but is not a complete geometric description. Direction count, face size, neck size, removable sectors and connected cushion-head box vary by product.
next_action: Retain MDO as an abbreviation and select a scheduled product form before drawing the face or airflow directions.

preferred_term: cushion-head box, linear-slot cushion-head box or terminal box according to the physical form
issue: These terms can describe different shaped transition volumes behind grilles and diffusers. A cushion head used in Australian flexible-duct installations is not automatically a central supply plenum, a North American boot or a pressure-independent terminal unit.
next_action: Store face connection, duct spigot, depth, taper and pressure-control equipment before treating terminal boxes as equivalent.

preferred_term: specified duct sealing tape, mastic, gasket or draw band by its declared function
issue: Duct tape can mean a generic cloth repair tape or a product intended for a particular duct material, insulation facing or vapour seal. Flexible-duct connections can require a draw band plus sealant or tape, not one universal adhesive strip.
next_action: Require substrate, joint type, sealing role and product evidence; do not select tape from appearance or nickname.

preferred_term: return-air grille for a mechanical return path and transfer-air grille for an opening between spaces
candidate_term: return vent, transfer grille or air grille
issue: A return grille connects a room to return ductwork or a return-air box. A transfer grille moves air between rooms or across a door or wall, often to provide make-up air. Their downstream paths and acoustic, fire and privacy implications differ.
next_action: Trace both sides of the opening before assigning return or transfer role.

preferred_term: closed-loop hydronic heating water pipe
candidate_term: hot-water pipe, heating pipe or warm-water line
issue: Hydronic heating water circulates through a heat source and emitters. Potable heated water is delivered to fixtures. The services may use similar pipe materials but have different water quality, valves, safety arrangements, temperatures and endpoints.
next_action: Require the fluid service and endpoints before selecting pipe, fittings, insulation or regulatory evidence.

preferred_term: R-value, airflow, pressure, capacity, clearance and acoustic performance as attributes or analysis linked to physical objects
candidate_term: R-value solid, airflow cone, compliant clearance box or capacity geometry
issue: These values describe material performance, operating state, design calculation or required empty space. A visible overlay can help coordination but is not a material quantity and cannot prove compliance from geometry alone.
next_action: Keep optional coordination overlays out of material take-off and link every claimed value to product, design and edition evidence.

preferred_term: AS 1668.2:2012 for the NCC Housing Provisions call-up and AS 1668.2:2024 only where the project adopts or otherwise uses it
issue: Standards Australia published a newer general ventilation edition, but publication does not silently replace the edition cited by the selected NCC pathway. A project can also be governed by jurisdictional transition or approval dates.
next_action: Persist the exact edition, NCC pathway, jurisdiction, project date and reason for use with every rule result.

preferred_term: refrigerant licence, authorisation, charging, evacuation and leak-test results as practitioner or work evidence
candidate_term: licensed pipe, compliant flare or certified air-conditioner geometry
issue: Australia regulates refrigerant handling and trading. Licences, work practices and test results concern people, businesses and completed work; they are not extra solids and cannot be inferred from a drawn tube, fitting or equipment box.
next_action: Attach licence and work records to installed instances without making compliance claims from shape.

preferred_term: documented condensate or cooler-water discharge point
candidate_term: drain to outside, stormwater, sewer or ground by default
issue: Acceptable discharge depends on equipment, drainage design, jurisdiction, site and connection conditions. Condensate and evaporative-cooler dump water also arise from different systems and may follow different requirements.
next_action: Require a selected discharge destination and connected plumbing or site object before completing the route.

preferred_term: volume-control, backdraft, fire, smoke and combination fire-smoke damper as separate roles
issue: The bodies can all contain blades, but their purposes, actuation, testing, access and evidence differ. A balancing or zone damper must never be substituted for a tested fire- or smoke-resisting penetration system.
next_action: Keep life-safety dampers in the fire-safety code path with tested-system evidence and use mechanical dampers only for airflow roles.

preferred_term: insulated flexible air duct for the complete product and inner core, insulation and outer jacket for its drawable layers
candidate_term: flex duct, duct liner or plastic duct
issue: The complete flexible duct is a layered product. Its helical inner core carries air, insulation provides thermal resistance and the outer jacket protects and contains the insulation. A torn jacket is not the same defect as a crushed inner core.
next_action: Generate the assembly by default but retain layer identity for cuts, damage, connections and material take-off.

preferred_term: manufacturer refrigerant branch joint for a simple split and branch box only where the selected multi-split architecture includes one
candidate_term: Y-piece, refnet, branch box or manifold
issue: A passive copper Y-joint and a boxed multi-port branch component are not the same object. Branch boxes can contain valves, electronics and several connection pairs, while a simple joint has only formed passages.
next_action: Read the selected equipment connection diagram before generating branches; add a branch-box product object only when confirmed.

preferred_term: evaporative cooling as an outdoor-air supply system with a documented building air-relief path
candidate_term: ducted cooling equivalent to refrigerated recirculating air conditioning
issue: A ducted evaporative cooler draws outdoor air through wet media and supplies it to rooms. The introduced air must leave the building through deliberate relief paths; closing the house like a recirculating refrigerated system changes performance and pressure behaviour.
next_action: Generate supply paths and request the designed relief strategy rather than adding a refrigerated-system return-air network.

preferred_term: hydronic flow and return as explicit circuit roles
candidate_term: two heating pipes, red pipe and blue pipe, supply and return inferred from position
issue: The same pipe product can serve either role and routes can cross. Colour, left-right position and relative elevation are conventions, not reliable system semantics.
next_action: Store direction and connected endpoints for every circuit segment instead of deriving role from display colour or coordinates.

preferred_term: buffer tank, expansion vessel and domestic storage water heater as separate vessel functions
issue: A buffer tank adds system water volume or hydraulic stability. An expansion vessel accepts thermal expansion against a gas cushion. A domestic storage heater contains potable water for fixture use. They have different ports, pressure behaviour, insulation and safety components.
next_action: Require vessel purpose, fluid, port arrangement and pressure data before selecting geometry or safety parts.

preferred_term: hydraulic separator or low-loss header only for a low-resistance primary-secondary interface
candidate_term: header, manifold, buffer tank or hydraulic separator
issue: All can appear as enlarged pipe bodies with several ports. A hydraulic separator decouples circuit flows; an ordinary header distributes branches; a manifold serves repeated circuits; a buffer tank stores significant water volume. Some products combine functions, but the roles are not automatic synonyms.
next_action: Store the hydraulic function and each port role; allow combined products only when supported by selected product evidence.

preferred_term: thermostatic radiator valve for local radiator modulation and room thermostat for an electrical zone demand
issue: A TRV head mechanically operates its own radiator valve in response to local temperature. A room thermostat sends a control request to valves, actuators, pumps or the heat source. They can coexist and have different placement and wiring.
next_action: Generate each physical control only when present and prevent furniture or covers from invalidating its intended sensing location.

preferred_term: one continuous underfloor-heating loop with paired flow and return manifold ports
candidate_term: floor-heating pipe grid, heating coil or floor zone
issue: A loop is a continuous pressure circuit, commonly without concealed intermediate joints, that leaves one flow port and returns to its matching return port. A room zone may contain several loops controlled together and is not itself a pipe object.
next_action: Keep circuit identity, continuous route, length, spacing and paired manifold ports explicit; treat zone grouping as control data.

preferred_term: gypsum plasterboard as the generic Australian object, with Gyprock as a proprietary search term and drywall as regional language
candidate_term: Gyprock, plasterboard and drywall as identical canonical product names
issue: Gyprock is a CSR trade mark that is widely used colloquially in Australia. Drywall is common North American language and can also refer to the wider construction method. Product brand, generic material and assembly must remain distinguishable.
next_action: Let all three terms find the object, retain plasterboard as the Australian generic name and keep the selected manufacturer and product separately.

preferred_term: lining for the wall or ceiling covering and separate trim, accessory and service objects attached to it
candidate_term: wall lining including skirting, cornice, architrave, switches and power points
issue: Attachments touch and visually complete a lined wall but have different materials, quantities, ownership and replacement. Treating every attachment as lining makes junction and take-off data unusable.
next_action: Connect trims, accessories and services to the lining with explicit relationships instead of merging their geometry or material identity.

preferred_term: selected plasterboard product and documented grade or system role
candidate_term: white board, green board, blue board, red board or acoustic board chosen by face colour
issue: Manufacturers use different colours and branded ranges. Water, fire, acoustic, impact and multi-performance properties belong to a selected product and complete system, not a universal colour code.
next_action: Require a product or explicit performance role; keep colour as appearance metadata only.

preferred_term: wall-lining furring channel, external cladding furring channel, acoustic resilient channel and ceiling furring channel as separate roles
issue: Similar cold-formed sections can support different faces, loads, clips and performance systems. A section name without host, orientation and role is not enough to select geometry or connections.
next_action: Ask for wall or ceiling, internal or external, support method and acoustic role before selecting a channel family.

preferred_term: direct-fixed ceiling for sheets or channels attached close to structure and suspended ceiling for a hanger-supported grid below it
candidate_term: dropped, battened, direct-fixed and suspended ceiling as interchangeable descriptions
issue: The systems have different load paths and parts. A direct-fix clip transfers load straight to nearby structure; a suspended grid requires anchors, hangers, primary and secondary members and restraint design.
next_action: Store the structural endpoint and support topology before generating the ceiling grid.

preferred_term: exposed-grid suspended ceiling, concealed suspended plasterboard ceiling or another named system
issue: Everyday terms describe a ceiling below the primary structure but do not say whether the finish is continuous plasterboard, removable lay-in tile, linear plank, baffle or another system.
next_action: Use false or drop ceiling for search, then request the visible finish and support system.

preferred_term: Level 3, 4 or 5 plasterboard finish as a specified finish requirement and inspection attribute
candidate_term: Level 5 material layer or Level 5 plasterboard object
issue: A level of finish describes the required jointing and surface preparation outcome under relevant viewing and decoration conditions. It is not an extra board or universally a single separate coating solid.
next_action: Attach the specified level, decoration, lighting and acceptance evidence to the complete lining surface; generate only the actual selected materials.

preferred_term: plasterboard back-block bonded behind a joint, sheet-edge backing fixed behind an edge, and framing nogging as separate members
candidate_term: back block, backing, blocking and nogging
issue: A plasterboard back-block spreads stress behind a joint. Edge backing provides a fixing surface. A nogging is part of wall framing. Their materials, positions and load paths differ.
next_action: Use material, face relationship, host and joint role to select the object; never infer it from the word block alone.

preferred_term: paper plasterboard tape, glass-mesh tape, fibre-cement tape, fire-system tape and acoustic-system tape as documented products
issue: The tapes can differ in material, alkali resistance, compound compatibility and tested-system role. Similar width or mesh appearance does not make them interchangeable.
next_action: Bind tape to board, compound and performance system; permit substitution only from explicit selected-system evidence.

preferred_term: external corner, internal corner, stopping, casing, shadowline and control-joint bead as separate profiles
